Semiconductor push advancing across capacity, key chips and design services: order visibility at Foxconn's 8-inch wafer fab in Japan now extends to Q4, and in-house silicon carbide, automotive MCU and AI power-IC programs are progressing on plan.

Greensboro, North Carolina fab (fifth InP fab, acquired March 2026): conversion from gallium arsenide to indium phosphide is 'well underway,' with long-pole items such as reactors already addressed. No change to schedule - first revenue in early 2028, ramping through calendar 2028 to full pitch by end of 2028 and into 2029. Capacity remains uncommitted and Lumentum is actively talking to customers about laser demand, expecting to announce new Greensboro arrangements (LTAs) over the next couple of quarters.
Greensboro GaAs-to-InP conversion underway; first revenue early 2028; ramp into 2029; LTAs in discussion

Advanced logic: shipped a system early in Q2 for a materials modification application supporting 2-nanometer production and a follow-on system in Q3 for the same application; continuing to work with this customer on its next-generation technology roadmap.
2 systems shipped for a 2-nanometer materials modification application

General mature: sales improved sequentially and customers are benefiting from AI data center applications manufactured on 28 nanometers and above (optical connectivity, microcontrollers, analog ICs); customers in China continue to add capacity and activity outside China is improving; growing interest in the new Purion H6 high current platform. CS&I strength driven by rising utilization in memory, silicon carbide and silicon power plus upgrade sales to floor-space-constrained customers.

Growth catalysts: GAA sales were about JPY 5 billion in Q1 and are expected at over JPY 20 billion for FY March 2027. Advanced packaging revenue, JPY 6 billion in FY March 2026, is now expected at JPY 15 billion in FY March 2027 (Q1 was JPY 4.5 billion) - a significant upward revision from the JPY 6 billion prior plan, driven by both rising customer CapEx and additional POR wins for its film deposition technology. In NAND, demand-supply is not fully adjusted - memory players are allocating clean room to DRAM while NAND wafer output needs to increase - so greenfield NAND investments are expected to resume, which converts all of Kokusai's PORs to sales and is broadly favorable. In DRAM, the D1C transition is complete and D1D is progressing. NAND sales could approach record highs, and DRAM plus NAND plus advanced packaging support growth above WFE (targeting more than a 20% sales increase).
GAA JPY 5 billion in Q1, over JPY 20 billion FY March 2027; advanced packaging raised to JPY 15 billion FY March 2027 from JPY 6 billion in FY March 2026

Revenue associated with ADVANCED LOGIC MORE THAN DOUBLED SEQUENTIALLY in Q2 as customers expanded production capacity, with demand stretching across product lines and divisions. The VeraFlex XPS materials-metrology platform kept gaining traction, driven by 'proliferation in gate-all-around manufacturers' as customers continue to INCREASE THE NUMBER OF VERAFLEX TOOLS PER FAB; XPS adoption is rising in logic, especially at the advanced nodes. Nova's AI-enabling modeling solution, combining physics-based and machine-learning algorithms, helps customers address the complex 3D device structures of gate-all-around and plays an increasingly important role in managing Nova's expanding GAA install base. An analyst characterised Nova as holding a position across ALL FOUR gate-all-around players and management did not dispute it, while declining to discuss any customer by name.
Advanced logic revenue more than doubled QoQ; VeraFlex tools per fab increasing at gate-all-around manufacturers; logic and foundry 73% of Q2 product revenue

The Nova WMC dimensional-metrology platform won a recent TOOL OF RECORD SELECTION BY A LEADING FOUNDRY CUSTOMER (not named on the call) for MULTIPLE LAYERS MEASUREMENT in advanced-packaging production flows. Nova is also seeing accelerating WMC adoption across BOTH memory and foundry customers, 'positioning us to benefit from further investment in advanced packaging and high-bandwidth memory manufacturing.' A new configuration of the Nova WMC extends its dimensional metrology capabilities to PANEL-LEVEL PACKAGING.

On PROCESS-CONTROL INTENSITY, management said it has to be broken down by end market because each behaves differently: LOGIC INTENSITY IS HIGHER THAN MEMORY, ADVANCED PACKAGING IS 'RAPIDLY GROWING,' and 3D NAND is currently muted in process control because its spend is upgrades rather than capacity expansion. Asked about the Terafab greenfield project, management declined to comment on any specific customer but said generically that PROCESS CONTROL INTENSITY AT THE INITIAL STAGES OF GREENFIELD FABS IS HIGHER THAN IN THE ONGOING OPERATIONS OF MORE MATURE FABS, because a new fab operator must improve time to market and reach the required yield threshold - citing the Rapidus build of a couple of years ago as an example of that pattern rather than as a Nova customer statement. The structural drivers - increasing complexity in architectures and materials - remain in place, and Nova points to customer adoption, market share gains and technology wins as its key indicators of outperformance.

Driver is new-product adoption rather than process-control intensity: the ATLAS G6 is being used for TRANSISTOR METROLOGY AT SEVERAL NODES BELOW 2nm, where its smaller spot size and tighter precision let customers apply OCD to parts of the wafer that previously required scribe-line test structures - a SAM/wallet-share expansion per 10k wafer starts. Iris films and integrated metrology are both on track for RECORD 2026 revenue, with integrated metrology in logic called pure share gain ('a year ago, we wouldn't have had hardly any, maybe zero logic for integrated metrology'). Iris G2 is in the normal 6-12 month install/qual/performance cycle; the Dragonfly G5 is being evaluated for FRONT-END applications against the incumbent, with bigger contribution expected in 2027. New FAST-technology applications aim to predict device performance earlier in the flow
Atlas G6 at several nodes below 2nm; Iris films + integrated metrology at record 2026 levels

Semiconductor vertical showed strong growth momentum driven by the AI flywheel: Siemens captured demand across its entire portfolio, including a wide-ranging ELECTRIFICATION WIN FOR A MAJOR NEW FAB PROJECT IN THE US, and announced at Computex an expansion of its partnership with Intel across the entire value chain from design to chip manufacturing. Digital Industries market environment supportive in electronics, semiconductors, aerospace and defense; DI revenue +10% with automation revenue +7% to EUR 3.1 billion and DI margin sharply improved to 18.7%.
Electrification win for a major new US fab project; DI revenue +10%, automation +7% to EUR 3.1 billion, DI margin 18.7%

AMD's 10-Q: AMD relies primarily on GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. (GF) for wafers for microprocessor and GPU products manufactured at process nodes larger than 7 nm, and is party to a wafer supply agreement under which GF provides a minimum annual capacity allocation to AMD and sets pricing through 2026. Besides TSMC, AMD also utilizes United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC) and Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. for its ICs in the form of programmable logic devices (process node not stated). Nearly all product assembly and final testing is performed at third-party operated manufacturing facilities in Mainland China, Malaysia and Taiwan.
GF wafer supply agreement: minimum annual capacity allocation and pricing through 2026

Semiconductor revenue was $554 million, up 19% sequentially and 28% year over year - a meaningful acceleration from 13% year-over-year growth in Q1 - and the Q3 guide implies year-over-year growth ACCELERATING TO OVER 50%. Within that, CEO John Lee said dep-etch is growing significantly faster than the over-50% average while litho, metrology and inspection have smaller ramp amplitudes; MKS is exposed to 85% of WFE. Full-year semiconductor growth of a little north of 35% was accepted as the right math. Design wins include being the PROCESS TOOL OF RECORD for dissolved gas applications in advanced logic and segment share leadership in RF POWER for high-aspect-ratio dielectric etch. Growth was broad-based across plasma and reactive gases, vacuum, power solutions, optics and photonics, with the last gaining momentum in lithography, metrology and inspection.
Semiconductor $554M (+19% QoQ, +28% YoY); Q3 implies >50% YoY growth; exposed to 85% of WFE; FY2026 semi growth a little north of 35%

Annealing delivered RECORD revenue across both the LSA and NSA product lines in Q2, with a projected annealing SAM of approximately $1.3 billion by 2030. Veeco remains the production tool of record for laser spike annealing at ALL THREE Tier 1 logic/foundry customers. On next-generation nanosecond annealing: a Tier 1 customer successfully completed its evaluation and placed a FOLLOW-ON ORDER for a second system shipping in the second half of 2026, and the third Tier 1 logic customer received an NSA evaluation tool - meaning Veeco has now engaged all three Tier 1 logic customers with NSA technology.
Record LSA and NSA revenue; annealing SAM ~$1.3B by 2030; production tool of record at all 3 Tier 1 logic customers; NSA follow-on order shipping H2 2026

Veeco remains the leader in ion beam deposition for EUV mask blanks and has extended its ion beam technology to EUV PELLICLES, which protect defect-free masks and improve productivity as EUV utilisation scales. It continues to win production business at a Tier 1 foundry and is engaging new customers for EUV pellicles, and is positioned as the industry advances toward high-NA lithography. Total ion beam deposition SAM is projected at approximately $500 million by 2030, driven by the IBD300 platform for low-resistance metals plus the EUV deposition leadership position.
IBD SAM ~$500M by 2030; EUV pellicle production wins at a Tier 1 foundry

Semiconductor Technologies net sales $744 million, up approximately 3% sequentially and 17% organically year-over-year, driven by demand strength especially for advanced logic and HBM chips; semi gross margin ~49% and adjusted operating EBITDA margin ~34% (right around 35% for the first half, expected to continue).
Semiconductor Technologies $744 million (+17% organic YoY); EBITDA margin ~34%

Advanced nodes portfolio grew more than 20% in Q2 (Investor Day plan was ~7%): continued growth at three nanometer, emerging activity at two nanometer, really strong pull for 2 nm and 18A, and successful scale-up of HBM3/HBM4 on the memory side; advanced nodes were about 40% of the portfolio exiting the first half versus the 45%-50% Investor Day target, which Qnity expects to reach early.
advanced nodes +20% YoY; ~40% of portfolio vs 45%-50% target

Fab utilization: advanced logic tracking to the mid-80% range, mainstream logic low 80%, DRAM high 80%, NAND low 80%; every wafer at advanced nodes requires more layers, more processing complexity and more packaging steps, translating to more Qnity content.
utilization: advanced logic mid-80%, mainstream logic low 80%, DRAM high 80%, NAND low 80%

CMP is the fastest-growing part of the semi portfolio (pads, cleans and slurries) with the most content gains plus incremental share gains on cleans and slurries; launched the Optivision Max soft polishing pad, already adopted at leading-edge nodes and in advanced packaging including AI and HBM-driven architectures; multiple POR wins at 16 and 14 (angstrom-era nodes) in the first half.

Lithography materials business continues to do really well; for the Qnity portfolio EUV matters less in the photoresist layer than in the ancillary layers around the photoresist, where it partners with customers to get the most out of their EUV investment. Kalrez (perfluoroelastomer seals) saw strong first-half growth on accelerated wafer fab equipment demand and is getting productivity, capacity release and automation initiatives.

Qnity is a consumables business correlated to wafer volume; MSI expected in the high single digits for 2026, with content outperformance considerably above MSI as all logic and memory leaders commercialize their most advanced technology simultaneously.

Semiconductor campus: the Northeast semiconductor project is running ahead of schedule with significant Q3 revenue expected, positioning Sterling 'as the go-to solution for large, complex projects' in semis; next wave of semiconductor plants seen around 2030, pharma 2028; initial scope awarded on an EV plant outside Atlanta.

Semiconductor revenue a record $278 million, +27% quarter-over-quarter and +33% YoY; 'The semiconductor equipment market is growing to record levels, driven by strong demand for leading-edge memory and logic, as well as increasing etch and dep intensity.' Shipping in line with underlying demand.

Second-half 2026 semiconductor revenue expected to grow almost 50% year-over-year, mostly from existing products with new products contributing more in 2027; 'We have good visibility into next year from our customer base in semiconductor.'

Plasma power share gains: eVerest and eVoS platforms validated for 'meaningful yield and throughput performance at the leading edge'; groundwork laid to gain share in conductor etch, dielectric etch and deposition across leading-edge logic, NAND and DRAM. AE is ahead of the $140 million share-gain target from its 2024 Analyst Day; system power wins in test, ALD and thermal sensing, with the system business on track to grow $40 million by 2030.
ahead of $140M share-gain target (2024 Analyst Day); system power business +$40M by 2030

Roughly 25% of the semiconductor business (service, circa high-teens/20% of plasma revenue, plus ion implant) does not track WFE; the goal remains to outgrow WFE over time, with mix of etch/dep vs other WFE segments driving year-to-year variation. Power density per tool is rising as voltages go up and fab floor space stays constrained.
~25% of semiconductor revenue not tied to WFE

For 2026 Ichor expects revenue growth in alignment with the high end of WFE expectations, an increase of at least 30% from full year 2025; the steepening customer demand ramp indicates sequential revenue growth exceeding 10% in each of the next two quarters and second half revenue volumes at least 25% higher than the first half. Demand drivers unchanged: advanced etch and deposition applications supporting AI infrastructure, gate-all-around architectures, advanced memory and leading-edge process technologies.
2026 revenue growth at least 30% vs 2025; H2 at least 25% above H1; >10% sequential growth in each of Q3 and Q4

Lithography customer: inventory position has been consistent and Ichor expects to burn through it as it exits Q3, with a return in Q4 and in Q1 in particular; the customer gives a long-range forecast and Ichor sees significant growth in 2027 with that customer, with litho picking up significantly in the first half of 2027 and being additive versus the second half of 2026.

WFE outlook: 2026 and 2027 WFE has more deposition and etch intensity; management sees a good chance the industry exceeds $200 billion WFE sometime in 2027 (range $190 billion up to $220 billion) and is preparing for the bull case, with EUV adoption in leading-edge foundry/logic and now memory also growing UCT business with smaller customers.
2027 WFE $190 billion-$220 billion, chance to exceed $200 billion

Services expected to grow double digits in 2026 and 2027, with acceleration after the ramp of factories in the U.S., improved utilization at one of its major customers in the U.S., and the planned leading-edge ramp in factories in Korea and Taiwan. Launched the first NPX Center of Excellence in Hillsboro, Oregon for earlier customer engagement on new products.

Management is decidedly more optimistic on H2 than at the Q1 call: the wafer-allocation doubts voiced in Q1 have eased because of the deep TSMC relationship ('we have more chance to get upside capacity'), and by late Q1/early Q2 the company found TSMC support and customers' capacity commitments much firmer. Cloud-related shipments (cloud compute, cloud training, cloud connectivity) were close to 80% of Q2 shipments with the remaining ~20% consumer/crypto/memory-related; the H2 mix should be similar, with crypto fading toward nothing and automotive ramping in its place. Versus last year, China's share of revenue declines (absolute volume still up), while the US share and Taiwan share both increase. Full-year gross margin: still confident, but dependent on customers' production ramp success and whether NRE tape-outs land this year or slip to next year.
cloud-related ~80% of Q2 shipments, other ~20%; H2 stronger than H1, no specific figure

→ TSMC: TSMC capacity support underpins the year: the Q1 wafer-allocation worry has flipped to optimism ('our TSMC roots are relatively deep, so we have more chance at upside capacity') and Q2's +20% QoQ was delivered on that support. Next year's wafer allocation is being opened by TSMC over the coming 1-2 months and management is very optimistic on GUC's share of it. The new chairman spent 29 years at TSMC and was appointed by TSMC, and GUC positions itself as TSMC's pure-play design-service arm (TSMC invested in GUC 23 years ago precisely to pair the foundry with a design house), co-optimizing DTCO and next-generation PPA with TSMC to win CSP sockets.

LEAP (leading-edge advanced packaging) revenue is tracking ~USD 200M AHEAD of the USD 3.5B 2026 guidance and management is aiming to DOUBLE LEAP revenue in 2027. Full-process CoWoS-like packaging is on track for ~USD 300M in 2026 with substantial growth in 2027 and is expected to be margin-accretive. ASE's fully automated PANEL line (310mm x 310mm) enters production in Q1 2027, complementary to foundry CoWoS and serving the same customer set at similar reticle size and pitch. Capacity — not demand — is the constraint: blended utilization 80-85% but effectively full, with growth gated by equipment installation and building construction (13 greenfield plus 8 brownfield projects underway). FY2026 capex raised USD 2B to ~USD 10.5B, ~70% of equipment capex going to leading edge.
LEAP ~USD 3.7B 2026, DOUBLING in 2027; full-process ~USD 300M; panel 310x310mm production Q1 2027

Technology roadmap. PANEL: ASE's fully automated panel line starts PRODUCTION IN Q1 2027 in a 310mm x 310mm form factor — described as COMPLEMENTARY to foundry CoWoS, serving the SAME CUSTOMER SET with identical reticle size and pitch/line-width coverage; adoption depends on capacity, performance and speed of execution. GLASS SUBSTRATE: NOT in production and not within the next 12 months; R&D is evaluating feasibility and economics with substrate suppliers, the foundry and customers. FULL-PROCESS (CoWoS-like): on track for ~USD 300M of revenue in 2026 with aggressive capacity expansion and substantial growth in 2027; margin not yet fully reflected but expected to be margin-accretive. CPO: launching toward the END OF 2026 in initially small volume, yielding benchmark data on bandwidth, system performance and thermal dissipation; more detail promised in two quarters. Bigger reticle sizes drive panel/more-complex CoWoS first, then POWER DELIVERY becomes the next constraint over the following two to three years.
panel 310x310mm production Q1 2027; glass substrate not within 12 months; full-process ~USD 300M 2026; CPO launches late 2026

Service-mix and competitive positioning. ASSEMBLY IS NOW KEEPING PACE WITH TEST: entering the year management expected test (led by rapid wafer-sort expansion) to outgrow assembly, but assembly has grown even more strongly than expected — 'especially as it relates to LEGACY WIRE BOND services' — so both are now expected to grow at similar rates in 2026 and in the 2027 LEAP mix. Computing applications keep rising as a share of ATM revenue, a trend management sees continuing into 2027 and 2028. On EMIB as a CoWoS alternative, Dr. Wu is deliberately agnostic: as a PURE-PLAY OSAT with 'no conflict with foundry, no conflict with substrate provider', 'if the EMIB substrate becomes the right alternative, we'll just buy EMIB substrate and we do the assembly' — not a zero-sum threat. U.S. footprint: test development and services in California with factories in Fremont and San Jose, extending to a third and fourth site; but manufacturing PROCESS development stays in Taiwan until scale and efficiency are proven, then migrates.
assembly now matching test growth (legacy wire bond strong); EMIB treated as pure-play-neutral

Traditional industrial gas backlog of approximately $3 billion in projects (FID-approved, long-term contracts); a significant portion of the capital projected for the backlog will support electronic customers, including over $1.5 billion in project wins for Air Products in the last six months. Two very large projects were announced, one in Korea and one in Taiwan, and other projects are to be announced this quarter.
backlog ~$3 billion; over $1.5 billion of project wins in last six months

CEO Eduardo Menezes: the market is going through a super cycle and the opportunity list is skewed to the electronic side - probably close to two-thirds of opportunities or more are in the electronic space; electronics is where the growth is, versus replacement-driven opportunities in chemicals and steel. Air Products kept the capability to execute electronics projects in Asia, which fits where the market is now.
close to two-thirds or more of opportunities in electronics

One very large multi-phase project in Taiwan started in 2022 is building more than five large air separation plants: three are done and two are still to go. All other backlog projects have basically come in the last 12 months.
Taiwan project: more than five large air separation plants, three done, two to go

RECORD REVENUE, GROSS PROFIT AND EPS, above the high end of the outlook: Q2 revenue $258.2M, +14.2% sequentially and +31.9% YoY, with HIGH BANDWIDTH MEMORY explicitly named (with co-packaged optics) as the key growth initiative driving the sequential increase in Probe Cards. GAAP gross margin 50.7%; GAAP EPS $0.71, non-GAAP EPS $0.82. The four-quarter arc CEO Mike Slessor cites: revenue +>30%, non-GAAP gross margin +1,500bps, EPS TRIPLED — 'years of investment to create and expand our unique position at the INTERSECTION OF HIGH-PERFORMANCE COMPUTE AND ADVANCED PACKAGING.' Q3 guided to ANOTHER RECORD: $270M +/- $10M with non-GAAP gross margin 54% +/- 1.5% and non-GAAP EPS $0.86 +/- $0.09, on strength in Foundry & Logic and Systems momentum.
Record $258.2M (+31.9% YoY); HBM + CPO named drivers; Q3 guide record $270M, non-GAAP GM 54%

CO-PACKAGED OPTICS TEST IS RUNNING AHEAD OF PLAN. FormFactor entered 2026 guiding $10-20M of CPO revenue, raised it to the high end a quarter ago, and now expects to EXCEED $20M BY THE END OF Q3 and to 'significantly exceed the $20 million level for the year overall'; systems-segment revenue nearly DOUBLED sequentially to a record $48.5M largely on this acceleration. Two drivers: growing CPO chip volumes planned for later this year, and leadership in 'the all-important TEST INSERTION ONE, which ensures KNOWN GOOD DIE on the PHOTONIC INTEGRATED CIRCUIT (PIC) wafer before it's combined with the electrical integrated circuit (EIC) to form the optical module in SCALE-UP AND SCALE-OUT network switches'. Management frames this as 'the very early stages of widespread adoption of silicon photonics in the broader semiconductor industry' as 'traditional copper interconnect is reaching physical limits in speed, heat and energy consumption', backed by a decade-long lab-to-fab first-mover advantage; served market sized at ~$400M by 2030. CPO revenue is recognized through the leading foundry (a 10% customer at 11% of Q2 revenue).
2026 CPO revenue to significantly exceed $20M (>$20M by end-Q3); ~$400M served market by 2030

RECORD REVENUE, GROSS PROFIT AND EPS, exceeding the high end of the outlook: Q2 (ended 06-27-2026) revenue $258.2M (+14.2% QoQ, +31.9% YoY); GAAP gross margin 50.7%; GAAP EPS $0.71 / non-GAAP $0.82 (versus $0.12 / $0.27 a year earlier). Broad-based demand with the two named growth initiatives — HIGH BANDWIDTH MEMORY (Probe Cards) and CO-PACKAGED OPTICS (Systems) — each driving sequential segment increases. Four-quarter transformation: revenue +>30%, non-GAAP gross margin +1,500bps, EPS TRIPLED, on FormFactor's position 'at the intersection of high-performance compute and ADVANCED PACKAGING'. Q3 guided to ANOTHER record: revenue $270M +/- $10M, non-GAAP gross margin 54% +/- 1.5%, non-GAAP EPS $0.86 +/- $0.09, with particular strength in FOUNDRY & LOGIC.
Record $258.2M, GAAP GM 50.7%, EPS tripled in 4 qtrs; Q3 record guide $270M / 54% GM

CALL-ONLY: THE CPU/GPU/ASIC PROBE-CARD LADDER, SPELLED OUT. Foundry & logic grew on data-center CPU demand as 'the trend of increasing CPU COMPUTE INTENSITY to enable AGENTIC AI use cases is now broadly appreciated'. Three distinct vectors: (1) incumbent share with 'a leader in data center CPUs'; (2) an expanding relationship with 'the world leader in high-performance compute', where a strong networking position is extending into that customer's GPU AND CPU product lines - FormFactor is QUALIFIED and 'shipping production units for revenue here in the THIRD QUARTER' (no GPU revenue was in Q2; the business is currently the competitor's); (3) qualification plus multiple design wins at 'a large fabless XPU customer', characterized as LOW SINGLE-DIGIT market share today with capacity commitments the near-term governor until Farmers Branch opens. HYPERSCALER CUSTOM ASICs are the next step-change: 'the next generation of something like a GOOGLE TPU is going to require an ADVANCED MEMS PROBE because of the power and speed requirements it runs at' - the same threshold crossing GPUs made two-to-four years ago - with little 2026 revenue but a key-supplier position expected as those parts ramp in 2027. Taiwan revenue +30% QoQ; the leading foundry was again a 10% customer (11%).
GPU probe cards qualified, production shipments start Q3; next-gen Google TPU needs advanced MEMS probe (2027)

→ TSMC: Taiwan revenue grew MORE THAN 30% SEQUENTIALLY in Q2 and 'the world's leading foundry was again a 10% customer' (11% of revenue) - FormFactor's probe cards and systems serving the intersection of high-performance compute and advanced packaging, where 'most of the manufacturing activity... is occurring in Taiwan'. CPO (co-packaged optics) revenue is recognized through this same 10% customer. To support 'the exceptionally steep ramps of complex devices like GPUs and custom ASICs', FormFactor expanded its multi-year partnership with Keystone Microtech (Zhubei, Taiwan) for local assembly and service capability.
value: 11% of Q2 revenue (10% customer); Taiwan revenue +30% QoQ

Record June quarter: revenue $6.72B (+15% QoQ, +30% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $1.82; September-quarter guide $8.1B (+>20% QoQ). DRAM = 23% of systems revenue. DRAM technology drivers: leveraging foundry-logic capabilities into DRAM PITCH SCALING — VECTOR hard-mask and diffusion-barrier tools 'critical for next-generation requirements'; Argos surface-treatment expanding into a growing set of DRAM applications; Equipment Intelligence / Dextro self-maintaining-tool solutions now expanding from NAND INTO DRAM. HBM-relevant: advanced packaging revenue on track for >70% YoY growth (raised from >50%) on TSV etch & electroplating leadership; AI driving 'more advanced DRAM and foundry architectures' and 'larger and more complex advanced packages'.
DRAM 23% of systems; VECTOR critical next-gen DRAM; adv packaging +>70% YoY

CALL — DRAM TO LEAD 2027 WFE: Lam expects DRAM to be the FASTEST-GROWING WFE segment in 2027 (then foundry/logic, then NAND — same order as 2026). June-quarter DRAM dollars were flattish AT THE RECORD March-quarter level (23% of systems revenue; 1-alpha/1-beta/1-gamma wafer additions + upgrades enabling DDR5/LPDDR5/HBM). Technology detail: DRAM customers adopting VECTOR hard mask for low-K film patterning (co-optimized with conductor etch; >20% COST SAVINGS vs traditional approaches) and VECTOR diffusion barriers (~5% CAPACITANCE REDUCTION vs competing tech); AKARA has won strategic tool-of-record positions including 'the most challenging GATE ETCH applications' in advanced DRAM. Thesis: 'as you push DRAM performance ahead, it starts to look A LOT LIKE LEADING-EDGE FOUNDRY LOGIC' — more EUV layers pull Lam's patterning etch, verticalization makes everything '3D-NAND-like.' HBM4/HBM4E raise capital intensity (taller stacks = longer process times + more equipment; unquantified). Down-payment rebound: deferred revenue +$213M QoQ largely on customer down payments.
DRAM = fastest WFE grower in 2027; Vector >20% cost save / ~5% capacitance cut; Akara advanced-DRAM gate-etch TOR wins

CALL — WHY NAND DOUBLED AND WHAT'S NEXT: the demand driver is AI itself — 'expanding CONTEXT WINDOWS and PERSISTENT MEMORY requirements are driving significantly higher demand for flash storage' — with conversions to 256+ layer-class devices primarily enabling ENTERPRISE SSDs. Lam's NAND SAM PER WAFER DOUBLES from the 128-layer node to 500+ layer devices (longer process times on taller stacks + additional tool steps). The ~$40B upgrade opportunity mostly completes BEFORE END-2027 — and then 'it all starts again' on a BIGGER installed base as the fleet steps 200 -> 300 -> 400 -> 500+ layers (greenfield adds meanwhile enlarge the base). On the TrendForce 2027 NAND-oversupply worry: customer conversations are still about upgrading the installed base; 'fundamentals are still about the same for us'; some greenfield this year but large-scale greenfield 'a ways out.' In the 2027 WFE mix NAND is the THIRD-fastest grower behind DRAM and foundry/logic — the same order as 2026, a year Lam is outperforming in.
NAND SAM/wafer 2x from 128L -> 500+L; $40B upgrades mostly pre-2028 then restart on bigger base; enterprise-SSD-led

RECORD June quarter (Q4 FY2026, ended 06-28-2026): revenue $6.72B (+15% QoQ, +30% YoY) — record revenue, operating margin AND EPS; non-GAAP gross margin 52.0% (+210bps QoQ), operating margin 38.4%, EPS $1.82. FY2026: revenue $23.23B (+26% vs $18.44B FY2025), EPS $5.82 (vs $4.13). September-quarter guide $8.1B +/- $400M — UP >20% SEQUENTIALLY — with GM 52%, OM 39.5%, EPS $2.15. CY2026 WFE now seen in the LOW $150B RANGE (up from the $140B view last quarter); third consecutive year of WFE outperformance; CY27+ called an 'extraordinary set-up' — customers have announced multi-year timelines for new fab projects. CEO Archer: 'AI-driven demand continues to reshape the semiconductor industry.' Mix: foundry 44% of systems revenue, memory 46% (DRAM 23% + NVM 23%); region Taiwan 27%, China 26%, Korea 20%. CSBG record $2.47B (+43% YoY). FCF $1.27B in Q; cash $5.6B; headcount ~22,400 (+1,800 QoQ).
Record $6.72B rev (+30% YoY), EPS $1.82; Sept guide $8.1B (+>20% QoQ); CY26 WFE low-$150B

Foundry-logic technology momentum: Argos surface-treatment winning customers at 2nm AND BELOW foundry-logic — surface-treatment applications roughly DOUBLE with gate-all-around (GAA); Akara conductor etch gaining momentum with installed-base growth expected to keep DOUBLING in CY27 (total conductor-etch installed base >40,000 chambers); VECTOR hard-mask/diffusion-barrier leverage from foundry-logic into DRAM. Advanced packaging now on track for >70% YoY revenue growth (raised from >50% last quarter) — leadership in TSV etch & electroplating, and PANEL-LEVEL PACKAGING tools shipping across multiple geographies. AI 'distinct waves' driving faster trajectory of Lam SAM toward HIGH-30s % of WFE.
Argos 2nm GAA wins; Akara base doubling CY27; adv packaging +>70% YoY; SAM -> high-30s % of WFE

Credo's 10-K describes a fabless model: in fiscal year 2026 Credo exclusively used TSMC for semiconductor wafer production and outsources all of its IC manufacturing to TSMC; after wafer fabrication it uses third-party contractors Amkor Technology and Advanced Semiconductor Engineering (ASE) for packaging its IC products, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC) and Sigurd Microelectronics for testing its IC products, and BizLink Technology for manufacturing its AEC products. Except for its agreement with BizLink for the manufacture of certain AEC products, Credo does not maintain long-term supply contracts with TSMC or its other contract manufacturers or suppliers; none of TSMC, BizLink or its other manufacturers or suppliers has provided contractual capacity assurances, and Credo has not entered capacity commitment arrangements with TSMC. It expects a transition to new foundry or assembly providers would take approximately 9 to 12 months.
approximately 9 to 12 months to transition foundry or assembly services to new providers

Product pipeline as described in the half-year report: (1) CUBE PROBER - HBM test equipment that fully inspects HBM at the individual-stack level with sub-5-micrometre vision precision, skipping the loader/unloader/COK tray steps by transferring wafers directly to the chuck; first Samsung HBM Cube Prober order won 2025-01 and a KRW 9,720M HBM test equipment supply contract with Samsung disclosed 2026-05-19; filing says the HBM market is led by SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron and that stacked-die (TSV) inspection difficulty is driving double-digit annual growth in memory ATE. (2) Probe stations TWP300 (in mass-production lines) and second-generation-vision TWP300H targeting localisation of a market dominated by Tokyo Electron and other Japanese vendors. (3) Burn-in chambers and sorters - started with overseas SSD burn-in, expanding to DRAM and non-memory; eSSD / PCIe 5.0-6.0 burn-in demand tied to AI data-center build-outs. (4) Memory, non-memory (SoC) and module/SSD test handlers plus change-over kits and interface boards sold as a handler-plus-board total solution. Filing frames test and inspection equipment as the fastest-growing equipment segment because HBM-style advanced packaging requires 100% inspection at each process step, raising both ASP and unit counts. AI / HBM framing in the half-year report (2026-08-14): the memory market is leading semiconductor growth on AI and big-data demand, and the equipment market is expected to keep growing over the medium-to-long term on the aggressive DRAM-centric investment memory makers are making to break the HBM SHORTAGE caused by the explosive expansion of AI end-markets. 2022-2024 is described as a harsh down-cycle (memory price collapse, utilisation drop); 2025-2030 is framed as a structural growth phase driven by generative-AI infrastructure build-out, led by HBM and sub-2nm foundry rather than commodity products. The AI-accelerator and HBM demand surge is forcing the equipment market onto a single high-end track where marginal technology or adequate tools have no place; foreign vendors from the US, Japan and Netherlands still hold the largest shares but Korean localisation is rising and the company's tools are now in mass-production lines of major customers at home and abroad, with overseas sales rising (China semiconductor revenue KRW 63,346M in H1 2026 vs KRW 42,017M in H1 2025). Order intake has accelerated sharply: MORE THAN $600 MILLION of orders received year to date, with deliveries scheduled through the remainder of 2026 and into 2027, materially improving visibility well into 2027. Approximately 80% of those orders are advanced packaging applications. OSATs accounted for MORE THAN 50% of total order intake, HBM players for OVER 20% of the $600 million (against the $260 million of POs and forecasts discussed on the prior call), and photonics for about 5%. Order flow started in Q1 and has grown steadily since. Most orders now being received are for 2027 rather than 2026, and management says a nice 2027 backlog is already building, with additional 2027 OSAT orders already in discussion.
>$600M orders year to date; ~80% advanced packaging; OSATs >50% of intake; HBM >20%; photonics ~5%

The HBM4 transition is a direct order driver: CEO Rafi Amit said 'the industry transition to HBM4 together with continued capacity expansion has resulted in significant orders from MULTIPLE LEADING HBM MANUFACTURERS.' In parallel, ongoing expansion of 2.5D and 3D IC packaging capacity is producing large multi-system orders from leading foundries, IDMs and OSATs. Within the HPC/AI portion of the business the two main segments are HBM and CoWoS (and CoWoS-like) applications, both expanding quickly and growing at roughly similar pace, with the faster one depending on which customers add capacity. Growth is attributed to a combination of share gains and genuine market capacity additions across HBM, CoWoS, fan-in and fan-out.

Advanced packaging mix is stepping up through the year: it was approximately 75% of Q2 revenue and is expected to reach around 80% by Q4. The advanced packaging business is expected to grow approximately 45% in the second half versus the first half, and Q4 advanced packaging revenue is expected to be approximately 70% HIGHER THAN Q1. HPC and AI-related products are already around 55% of revenue and may reach closer to 60% by the end of the year, with conventional advanced packaging roughly another 20%. Non-advanced-packaging business is stable with modest growth, helped by significant CMOS image sensor orders and early signs of recovery in consumer-related areas.
Advanced packaging ~75% of Q2 revenue rising to ~80% by Q4; AP +45% H2 vs H1; Q4 AP ~70% above Q1; HPC/AI ~55% of revenue rising toward ~60%

Electroplating momentum on both front-end and back-end: in logic, larger die sizes and steadily higher interconnect layer counts; in memory, HBM packaging demands higher levels of DRAM stacking and thus more copper process steps. ACM shipped its 2,000th electroplating chamber in the quarter (500th in 2022, 1,500th in 2025); the copper plating market is now almost $1.5 billion, with backside power and HBM DRAM stacking driving more plating tool demand.
2,000th electroplating chamber shipped; copper plating market almost $1.5 billion

Memory is expected to show strong year-over-year growth in 2026 with momentum into 2027 as customers accelerate clean room investments to support growing DRAM and high-bandwidth memory demand driven by AI; 2026 is a significant improvement over the low 2025 base with significant DRAM memory revenue, and second-half memory revenue probably looks similar to the first half because customers are solving bottlenecks in existing fabs until new clean room space comes online.

Memory customer portfolio is expanding: a recent order for multiple high current systems in the current quarter, and additional orders from the leading North American memory manufacturer (referenced last quarter) after the successful completion of its system evaluation, to support new fab investments. High current is the important implant category for memory; medium current also competitive; high energy has less memory content.

2027 memory: too early to size, indications are another year of growth but at a much lower percentage growth rate than 2026 given the low 2025 base; customers have ambitious capacity plans and Axcelis is expanding beyond its traditional position into other areas of the memory market and other customers. An analyst inferred about $120 million of annual memory run rate from the second-half-similar-to-first-half comment (analyst estimate, not confirmed by management).
no specific figure (analyst estimate ~$120 million annual memory run rate)

NAND: a little activity but no trend yet; anyone with clean room space is using it for higher-value DRAM. Vertical scaling of NAND does not change implant density, so NAND only helps Axcelis when customers add wafer capacity; historically NAND has followed DRAM. Memory systems carry lower-than-corporate-average gross margin but drive higher-margin CS&I aftermarket over the tool life.

Memory: despite the anticipated sequential decline from a strong Q1, customer engagement remains robust; strong year-over-year growth expected in 2026 with momentum into 2027 as customers accelerate clean room investments to support DRAM and high-bandwidth memory demand driven by AI. Recent order for multiple high current systems in the current quarter, and additional orders from the leading North American memory manufacturer after its system evaluation, to support new fab investments.

Growth catalysts: GAA sales were about JPY 5 billion in Q1 and are expected at over JPY 20 billion for FY March 2027. Advanced packaging revenue, JPY 6 billion in FY March 2026, is now expected at JPY 15 billion in FY March 2027 (Q1 was JPY 4.5 billion) - a significant upward revision from the JPY 6 billion prior plan, driven by both rising customer CapEx and additional POR wins for its film deposition technology. In NAND, demand-supply is not fully adjusted - memory players are allocating clean room to DRAM while NAND wafer output needs to increase - so greenfield NAND investments are expected to resume, which converts all of Kokusai's PORs to sales and is broadly favorable. In DRAM, the D1C transition is complete and D1D is progressing. NAND sales could approach record highs, and DRAM plus NAND plus advanced packaging support growth above WFE (targeting more than a 20% sales increase).
GAA JPY 5 billion in Q1, over JPY 20 billion FY March 2027; advanced packaging raised to JPY 15 billion FY March 2027 from JPY 6 billion in FY March 2026

ADVANCED PACKAGING set a record and contributed nearly one-quarter - 'nearing 25%' - of overall product revenue in Q2, driven by the dimensional metrology portfolio and fuelled by customers' continued investment in advanced packaging and HIGH-BANDWIDTH MEMORY capacity to support AI-related device demand. Nova had guided advanced packaging to between 20 and 25% of product revenue for the year and now sees it 'inching towards the 25% for the year.' Management frames advanced packaging as a MULTI-YEAR STRUCTURAL growth opportunity that has gone from essentially no revenue several years ago to a meaningful contributor, now spanning optical, chemical AND materials metrology, and becoming increasingly similar to front-end manufacturing in complexity across both logic and memory. Chiplets, HYBRID BONDING, PANEL-LEVEL PACKAGING and 2.5D integration all increase both the number of measurements required and their criticality; hybrid bonding is described as 'an additional layer that will accelerate this growth for Nova.'
Advanced packaging a record at nearly 25% of Q2 product revenue, inching toward 25% for the full year (initially guided 20-25%)

The Nova WMC dimensional-metrology platform won a recent TOOL OF RECORD SELECTION BY A LEADING FOUNDRY CUSTOMER (not named on the call) for MULTIPLE LAYERS MEASUREMENT in advanced-packaging production flows. Nova is also seeing accelerating WMC adoption across BOTH memory and foundry customers, 'positioning us to benefit from further investment in advanced packaging and high-bandwidth memory manufacturing.' A new configuration of the Nova WMC extends its dimensional metrology capabilities to PANEL-LEVEL PACKAGING.

Memory and others was 27% of Q2 product revenue and Nova projects MEMORY AT ABOUT 30% for full-year 2026, a slight increase on the 70/30 logic-to-memory ratio of 2025, against a long-term model of about 60/40 in favour of logic because process-control intensity in logic is higher. The MAJORITY OF NOVA'S MEMORY EXPOSURE IS DRAM, where demand is strong, while 3D NAND remains 'somehow muted' this year because its growth is driven by UPGRADES rather than capacity expansion - even though metrology intensity between DRAM and NAND is 'more or less similar.' Nova sells to ALL THE TOP PLAYERS IN THE NAND MARKET (positions vary by product line) and expects to benefit once NAND capacity investment returns, which management hopes will be sometime next year. Coming DRAM technology transitions - 4F-squared, 6F-squared, advanced DRAM architectures and eventually 3D DRAM - all increase process complexity and metrology requirements. A new generation of the Nova PRISM platform is targeted at advanced memory structures.
Memory 27% of Q2 product revenue and ~30% expected for 2026 (2025 was 70/30); long-term model 60/40 logic/memory; DRAM strong, 3D NAND muted and upgrade-driven

HBM is one of the two engines behind 30% QoQ growth in the Dragonfly-led inspection business (the other being 2.5D logic): 'For sure, it's HBM, where we've seen really phenomenal growth in both 2D inspection as well as 3D metrology', plus pickup from 3Di and new applications for SUB-SURFACE INSPECTION, which 'becomes more critical for 3D or heterogeneous packaging applications'. Demand across advanced packaging is strongest from HBM MANUFACTURERS and OSATs, driving the full-year advanced-packaging growth outlook up to ~80% (from ~50%). HBM and 2.5D have grown at a similar pace all half, and HBM 'is continuing to be pretty strong' into H2
inspection +30% QoQ on 2.5D + HBM; adv packaging FY26 ~+80%

ADVANCED PACKAGING FULL-YEAR GROWTH OUTLOOK RAISED TO ~80%, up from the ~50% projected just one quarter earlier. Demand is strongest from HBM MANUFACTURERS and OSATs supporting heterogeneous packaging for AI. adv packaging FY26 ~+80% (was +50%); >$200M single-OSAT Dragonfly order (mostly 2027)

THE NPO / SCALE-UP THESIS AND THE III-V ROADMAP: SiPho pluggables (800G/1.6T) have 'for the most part ALREADY REPLACED COPPER for scale-out connections outside the rack'; the NEXT FRONTIER IS SCALE-UP, where Tower has SEVERAL NEAR-PACKAGED-OPTICS (NPO) DEPLOYMENTS PLANNED OVER THE NEXT YEAR and many more in design — NPO expected to be 'in the TENS OF PERCENT' of SiPho shipments by H2 2027 (it reuses the pluggable ecosystem, easing hyperscaler reliability/serviceability/multi-source concerns). Content growth comes from HETEROGENEOUS INTEGRATION: III-V-on-silicon INTEGRATED InP LASERS (several tens of $M of revenue expected in 2027; chip-to-wafer bonding moving in-house), die-to-wafer/wafer-to-wafer bonding, and next-gen modulators (400G/lane silicon with Coherent; TFLN and InP in development); multi-year IQE EPI SUPPLY AGREEMENT resolved the InP-substrate crunch. SiGe: 100G/200G-per-lane drivers and TIAs in HVM across all three 200mm fabs (pluggables + LPO/LRO), 400G/lane next with tight EIC-PIC co-design. Adjacent read-through: image-sensor demand SURGING for machine-vision inspection driven by 'the accelerated build-out of DDR and HBM MEMORY ASSEMBLY LINES.'
NPO = tens-of-% of SiPho shipments by H2-2027; integrated InP lasers = tens of $M in 2027; pluggables already displaced copper for scale-out

Memory $34M (+8.8% QoQ); ~40% of the NAND market goes to data centers

Technology and product: BiCS8 ramped to the MAJORITY of bit production this year across both TLC and QLC, enabled by CBA hybrid wafer bonding; BiCS10 announced and in ramp plans for FY2027 capex. The QLC STARGATE platform BEGAN SHIPPING FOR REVENUE this quarter, completing a portfolio spanning performance-intensive compute (TLC enterprise SSD, scaled across a broad set of hyperscale and AI infrastructure customers) and high-capacity AI data lakes. Supply grows primarily through NODAL TRANSITIONS rather than wafer additions. High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) advanced: a global standard was announced with SK Hynix, advisory-board additions were made, and HBF performance simulations were shown at the FMS keynote; shipping and release dates not yet disclosed. NVIDIA's context-memory CMX standard and Storage NEXT plans were both characterized as opportunities.
BiCS8 majority of bits; BiCS10 announced; QLC Stargate first revenue; HBF standard with SK Hynix

→ SK Hynix: Sandisk and SK Hynix announced a GLOBAL STANDARD for High Bandwidth Flash (HBF), the emerging flash tier aimed at changing the AI memory-storage hierarchy for inference. Sandisk first announced HBF about eighteen months ago; it has since added members to its HBF advisory board and showed HBF performance simulations at its FMS keynote, with significant customers publicly discussing the technology. Shipping and release dates were not disclosed on the call.

Memory is described as a significant long-term growth opportunity as AI compute architectures accelerate DRAM and NAND demand and create new thermal processing and material requirements. Veeco is the production tool of record at A TIER 1 HIGH-BANDWIDTH MEMORY MANUFACTURER that is accelerating its investments in 2026. An LSA evaluation is advancing at a second Tier 1 DRAM customer with potential follow-on orders in the 2027-2028 timeframe, and engagement is expanding with a third DRAM customer that could enter an evaluation agreement over the coming quarters. Several NAND customers are exploring LSA and NSA applications. Separately, multiple IBD300 systems are under evaluation for advanced DRAM applications such as bit line metallization. The memory industry is at the early stages of adopting laser-based annealing.
Production tool of record at a Tier 1 HBM manufacturer accelerating 2026 investment; LSA evaluation at a second Tier 1 DRAM customer; multiple IBD300 systems in DRAM evaluation

CALL — HELIOS RAMP AND ECONOMICS: Helios is IN PRODUCTION with initial shipments beginning later in Q3, a step-up in Q4, a FURTHER step-up in Q1 2027, and a ramp through 2027; customer pull is 'very strong and TRACKING AHEAD OF OUR INITIAL FORECASTS' (a volume statement, per Lisa Su). Across inferencing workloads Helios delivers UP TO 15% MORE THROUGHPUT AT THE SAME RACK POWER and UP TO 30% MORE TOKENS PER DOLLAR than the competition, and carries ~50% more HBM than competing racks. Yields on the highly complex product are expected to improve over the next few quarters. Beyond the gigawatt-scale anchors (OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic — consuming via multiple CSPs), 'lots of customers' are interested at more regular scale, with good customer diversity expected by Q4/Q1. New Cerebras partnership: Helios plus Cerebras' Wafer Scale Engine forms a disaggregated FAST-INFERENCE solution available in Q4 in the Cerebras Cloud, extending into 2027. Supply: 'we have supply to more than meet the guidance... and the upside potential is there'; no data-center readiness constraint (land/power/shell) that threatens targets, though the range depends on how fast operators bring capacity online.
Helios: production now, ships late Q3 -> Q4 step-up -> Q1'27 step-up; +15% throughput/same power, +30% tokens/$; pull ahead of forecast

Helios carries ~50% MORE HBM THAN THE COMPETITION — a deliberate TCO advantage for large-model inference. AMD has worked with memory partners for multiple years and has 'very good visibility into HBM ALLOCATION for what we expect to deliver in 2027' (multi-year agreements). In the current memory-cost environment every customer is optimising memory footprint, and AMD retains the flexibility to MODIFY THE HBM FOOTPRINT per workload where the TCO benefit is smaller (medium-sized models) — the memory benefit is workload-dependent.
Helios ~50% more HBM vs competition; multi-year HBM allocation visibility into 2027; footprint modifiable per workload

CALL — CXL REVIVAL, TAURUS EXPANSION, CUSTOM SILICON: CXL momentum is back, driven by (1) MEMORY PRICING/SUPPLY dynamics — CXL-attached memory as a cost alternative to expensive local memory/HBM for memory-intensive inference and agentic workloads, (2) GPU-attach with KV-CACHE ACCELERATION improving inference latency, (3) memory-intensive general compute (SAP-class). Closed a NEW standard Leo design win at a U.S. hyperscaler in Q2; in 2027 expects VOLUME shipments of BOTH standard and custom Leo CXL controllers to TWO U.S. HYPERSCALERS. Taurus: 100G/lane smart cable modules in pre-production for 800G AECs; new 3.2T smart retimers/redrivers at 200G/lane (first with 'smart swap') support next-gen Ethernet AND UALink and DOUBLE the Taurus TAM to OVER $4 BILLION by 2030. Custom: NVLINK FUSION-BASED designs for hybrid rack architectures plus custom Leo controllers — initial shipments 2027, 'multi-billion dollar incremental opportunity.' On NAND supply: 'we still able to get supply, but unfortunately supply not enough to what we need... We have supply, but supply still not enough what we need.' Phison met every NAND supplier at FMS last week and pitched that its purchases feed its own AI data-platform systems, not just module resale; it will not disclose how many LTAs it holds so competitors cannot ask for the same amounts. CEO expects the NAND shortage to continue into next year and beyond ('many year'); a top NAND-maker executive told him a new fab takes 4 years from investment to production, not 2. Downgrade-grade NAND supply is also shrinking structurally: 3D NAND yields now run 90-plus percent, with some wafers at 95% good die, so the cheap downgrade bin that used to feed consumer products is disappearing.

Demand is too strong, so price will keep rising but at a decelerating rate toward saturation, at which point suppliers start choosing whom to ship. On demand structure: systems have cut DRAM content ('a lot of systems, they cut half of the DRAM') but nobody cuts storage - inference needs storage, 'storage is money' - and aiDAPTIV uses flash to complement DRAM.
