I don't think we get out of it as an industry TILL 2028,' but Arista's specific H1 actions pay off in H2: MULTI-YEAR PURCHASE COMMITMENTS NEARLY TRIPLED YoY to $9.7 BILLION (from $3.6B; $8.9B in Q1); MEMORY SUPPLY SECURED FOR 2026 with visibility WELL INTO 2027 (DDR4/DDR5/NAND); PCB + optics capacity buildable in a 12-month window; a NEW LIQUID-COOLING SUPPLY CHAIN stood up (cold plates, quick disconnects, tubing with capacity agreements); 3 CMs + 3 distribution hubs (US/Asia/Mexico). Guidance is explicitly supply-gated: 'guiding based on what we're CONFIDENT we can get the supply for — if supply released more, there is opportunity to do better.' Price increases only help 'end of the year or more like next year' (backlog); FY GM held 62-64% including memory/silicon cost inflation. Etherlink AI-fabric customers now EXCEED 100 CUMULATIVE (from 4-5 in 2024).
FY26 raised to ~$12.6B (+40%, 3rd raise); purchase commitments ~3x YoY to $9.7B; memory secured into 2027; liquid-cooling chain built; >100 AI customers

Fab utilization: advanced logic tracking to the mid-80% range, mainstream logic low 80%, DRAM high 80%, NAND low 80%; every wafer at advanced nodes requires more layers, more processing complexity and more packaging steps, translating to more Qnity content.
utilization: advanced logic mid-80%, mainstream logic low 80%, DRAM high 80%, NAND low 80%

Magnetic Application Products: net sales JPY 81.6 billion +49.6% YoY, operating profit JPY 9.6 billion +51.8% - HDD market demand remains strong on expanding AI data center demand; HDD head shipment volume +36% and HDD suspension shipment volume +31% YoY (QoQ heads +12%, suspensions +8%). R&D expenses rising in the HDD head business advancing next-generation technologies such as HAMR. Sensor Application Products sales JPY 61.9 billion +33.3% with OP JPY 7.8 billion (~3x); Energy Application Products sales JPY 405.8 billion +42.1% with OP JPY 69.4 billion +25.3% (small-battery price adjustments, battery pack expansion, mid-sized industrial batteries; JPY 2.6 billion one-time gain on EV power supply business transfer).
Magnetic sales JPY 81.6 billion +49.6%; HDD head shipments +36%, suspensions +31% YoY on AI data center demand

Product momentum in FY2027: coater developer (share of more than 90% across EUV to immersion lithography) won PORs in multiple processes in advanced logic and DRAM with the new Resive Pro Dice; full-year etch system sales of JPY 1 trillion are coming within reach; cryogenic etch systems for 400-layer NAND start deploying in customers' mass production lines from calendar 2027; a POR was won for a new low resistance metal deposition system in a new application area. For DRAM interconnect etch, five-year cumulative sales to fiscal 2030 are getting closer to JPY 1 trillion, significantly exceeding the original guidance of JPY 500 billion. In advanced packaging, prober sales show outstanding growth with full-year sales likely to go significantly beyond JPY 100 billion, and the Prexa SDP device prober for advanced logic launched in April; bonder/debonder and 3D-IC are growth areas combining leading-edge front-end and bonding technology.

Coater developer share more than 90%; etch sales JPY 1 trillion full-year within reach; DRAM interconnect etch five-year cumulative sales near JPY 1 trillion vs JPY 500 billion original guidance; prober sales significantly beyond JPY 100 billion; cryogenic etch for 400 layers in mass production from calendar 2027

AI data center applications drive the WFE market: sales to AI data center are expected to grow by five times or more in the five years from calendar 2023 through calendar 2027, spanning not only GPU and HBM but also DDR, CPU and 3D NAND. Technology transitions expected within two years: logic scaling from the 3 nanometer mainstream toward 2 nanometer with backside PDN adoption, DRAM evolving to the 1D node (1C to 1D transition), HBM stacked DRAM count rising from 12 to 16, and NAND evolving to 300 layers and further to 400 layers. Agentic AI is the driver of the overall WFE market; CY2026 WFE application mix is about 60% logic and 40% memory, versus 65%/35% last year.
AI data center WFE sales to grow five times or more CY2023-CY2027; HBM stacks from 12 to 16; NAND to 300 then 400 layers; logic mainstream 3 nanometer moving to 2 nanometer

CALL — TRAINIUM MERCHANT-SILICON DOOR OPENS; OWN FRONTIER MODEL: 'An increasing number of customers are interested in us providing the Trainium chips to them, SEPARATE FROM OUR CLOUD, and we're actively having those conversations... I expect there's a REAL CHANCE we'll do that in the future' (Jassy). Trainium adopter list broadened beyond the Anthropic + OpenAI multi-year multi-gigawatt anchors: unicorns Neurorobotics and Odyssey join Twelve Labs, Descartes Labs, Poolside AI, Karakuri, Metagenomi, NetoAI and Splash Music, plus Uber and Pinterest. AI-pulls-core mechanism: post-training reinforcement learning and AGENT TOOL USE run mostly on CPUs → Graviton (30-40% better price-performance; Graviton5 ramping ~2x faster than Graviton4). Amazon IS pursuing its OWN FRONTIER MODEL — for cost control, training-priority control and speed — while keeping Bedrock model-agnostic: 'within the next few years you're going to have at least a half dozen models comparably good to each other... one of them will be ours.' Agentic layer: Kiro coding agent usage TRIPLED QoQ (up to 50% more cost-effective); AWS Continuum security agent launched (finds/validates/remediates code vulnerabilities); Bedrock Agents added policies, payments, web search. Amazon Leo: ~400 satellites in orbit, initial internet service THIS YEAR with 'meaningful revenue commitments' from enterprises/governments. Memory/HDD/SSD inflation: existing contracts keep agreed prices for their duration; NEW deals price in current component costs.
Trainium sales OUTSIDE the cloud 'a real chance'; own frontier model coming ('one of the half dozen will be ours'); Kiro 3x QoQ

Record June quarter: revenue $6.72B (+15% QoQ, +30% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $1.82; September-quarter guide $8.1B (+>20% QoQ). DRAM = 23% of systems revenue. DRAM technology drivers: leveraging foundry-logic capabilities into DRAM PITCH SCALING — VECTOR hard-mask and diffusion-barrier tools 'critical for next-generation requirements'; Argos surface-treatment expanding into a growing set of DRAM applications; Equipment Intelligence / Dextro self-maintaining-tool solutions now expanding from NAND INTO DRAM. HBM-relevant: advanced packaging revenue on track for >70% YoY growth (raised from >50%) on TSV etch & electroplating leadership; AI driving 'more advanced DRAM and foundry architectures' and 'larger and more complex advanced packages'.
DRAM 23% of systems; VECTOR critical next-gen DRAM; adv packaging +>70% YoY

CALL — DRAM TO LEAD 2027 WFE: Lam expects DRAM to be the FASTEST-GROWING WFE segment in 2027 (then foundry/logic, then NAND — same order as 2026). June-quarter DRAM dollars were flattish AT THE RECORD March-quarter level (23% of systems revenue; 1-alpha/1-beta/1-gamma wafer additions + upgrades enabling DDR5/LPDDR5/HBM). Technology detail: DRAM customers adopting VECTOR hard mask for low-K film patterning (co-optimized with conductor etch; >20% COST SAVINGS vs traditional approaches) and VECTOR diffusion barriers (~5% CAPACITANCE REDUCTION vs competing tech); AKARA has won strategic tool-of-record positions including 'the most challenging GATE ETCH applications' in advanced DRAM. Thesis: 'as you push DRAM performance ahead, it starts to look A LOT LIKE LEADING-EDGE FOUNDRY LOGIC' — more EUV layers pull Lam's patterning etch, verticalization makes everything '3D-NAND-like.' HBM4/HBM4E raise capital intensity (taller stacks = longer process times + more equipment; unquantified). Down-payment rebound: deferred revenue +$213M QoQ largely on customer down payments.
DRAM = fastest WFE grower in 2027; Vector >20% cost save / ~5% capacitance cut; Akara advanced-DRAM gate-etch TOR wins

NAND revenue DOUBLED SEQUENTIALLY in the June quarter (NVM = 23% of systems revenue) — the NAND upgrade/conversion cycle is now converting to revenue at scale. Record total revenue $6.72B (+15% QoQ, +30% YoY), EPS $1.82; September guide $8.1B (+>20% QoQ). AI driving 'more flash storage demand'; Lam expecting continued growth in SAM PER WAFER in NAND; high-aspect-ratio (HAR) structures: conductor-etch installed base >40,000 chambers, Akara gaining momentum with installed base expected to keep doubling in CY27. Dextro: automated preventive-maintenance tasks DOUBLED since start of CY2026; Equipment Intelligence/Dextro rollout in 'very early stages' across the installed base, expanding from NAND into DRAM.
NAND revenue 2x QoQ (NVM 23% of systems); SAM/wafer growing; Akara doubling CY27

CALL — WHY NAND DOUBLED AND WHAT'S NEXT: the demand driver is AI itself — 'expanding CONTEXT WINDOWS and PERSISTENT MEMORY requirements are driving significantly higher demand for flash storage' — with conversions to 256+ layer-class devices primarily enabling ENTERPRISE SSDs. Lam's NAND SAM PER WAFER DOUBLES from the 128-layer node to 500+ layer devices (longer process times on taller stacks + additional tool steps). The ~$40B upgrade opportunity mostly completes BEFORE END-2027 — and then 'it all starts again' on a BIGGER installed base as the fleet steps 200 -> 300 -> 400 -> 500+ layers (greenfield adds meanwhile enlarge the base). On the TrendForce 2027 NAND-oversupply worry: customer conversations are still about upgrading the installed base; 'fundamentals are still about the same for us'; some greenfield this year but large-scale greenfield 'a ways out.' In the 2027 WFE mix NAND is the THIRD-fastest grower behind DRAM and foundry/logic — the same order as 2026, a year Lam is outperforming in.
NAND SAM/wafer 2x from 128L -> 500+L; $40B upgrades mostly pre-2028 then restart on bigger base; enterprise-SSD-led

CALL — THE 2027 WFE SETUP: 'probably eight, nine, 10 NEW FABS coming online between now and the end of next year'; the industry is 'MEANINGFULLY UNDERSUPPLIED' rolling into 2027, and customers are securing equipment orders for new clean-room space AT LEAD TIME OR BEYOND. The $140B->low-$150B CY26 WFE raise came from customers SQUEEZING OUT extra clean-room space and resolving bottleneck tools — further in-year upside is now hard, so discussions have moved to 2027 fab-fill. On sequential growth every quarter through end-2027: 'I feel incrementally good about each successive quarter.' 2027 growth order repeats 2026: DRAM fastest, foundry/logic second, NAND third. Lam is 'talking to that NEW LOGIC CUSTOMER IN THE U.S.' (unnamed). China WFE flat to slightly up — multinationals' China fabs GREW while domestic customers declined (China 26% of revenue). KEY RATIO UPDATED: ~$100B of data-center capex ≈ ~$8B of WFE, now 'trending a billion or two higher' (~$9-10B per $100B) — hyperscale investment 'trickling all the way back to WFE.'
8-10 new fabs by end-2027; industry undersupplied; orders at lead time+; $100B DC capex -> ~$9-10B WFE (raised)

NAND/DRAM scarcity is the defining constraint. CEO Wallace Kou: the AI super cycle has driven substantial HBM, DRAM, NAND and HDD price increases and 'mounting substrate and supply pressure,' and he expects the scarcity to persist 'likely until 2028 when new fabs come online.' DRAM and NAND now account for almost 56% of total BOM cost on a low-end smartphone, forcing OEMs to trim specifications; smartphone units are still expected down 10-15% in 2026. NAND makers are redirecting focus and CapEx to DRAM and HBM, deemphasising eMMC/UFS and exiting automotive - which hands share to Silicon Motion's module-maker customers and gives it stronger pricing power. Long-standing relationships let Silicon Motion secure NAND from multiple suppliers through the shortage, which management calls a significant and enduring differentiator.
NAND scarcity expected to persist until 2028; DRAM+NAND ~56% of low-end smartphone BOM; smartphone units -10% to -15% in 2026

MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers entered commercial production in Q2 with TWO Tier 1 customers, with five additional Tier 1 customers expected to ramp in the second half. Management reaffirmed the target of 5-10% of total revenue coming from MonTitan exiting 2026. First customers are targeting the compute market with TLC NAND for AI platforms that use NAND for high-speed, low-latency storage dedicated to NEAR-GPU AND NEAR-CPU KV CACHE. TLC-based solutions are ramping ahead of QLC: early QLC shipments begin late 2026 but QLC only becomes meaningful late 2027 into 2028, gated by the availability and affordability of 2-terabit QLC dies. CFO Jason Tsai was explicit that the delay is a NAND-industry availability issue, not a controller issue.
2 Tier 1 customers in production, 5 more ramping in H2; MonTitan targeted at 5-10% of revenue exiting 2026

Next-generation 4-nanometer PCIe Gen 6 MonTitan controller completes tape-out in August 2026, developed in close collaboration with customers and aimed at hyperscalers and cloud service providers. Multiple design wins are already secured with both flash makers and cloud service providers, and more than a dozen Tier 1 customers are waiting for samples. The architecture targets AI inference - management specifically cited NVIDIA's CMX architecture - plus multi-host operation under new AI workloads. Management expects the Gen 6 ramp to be 'much stronger and faster, bigger than our PCIe Gen 5 ramps' and set an initial target market share of at least 15-20%, with the controller becoming a significant growth driver in 2028.
4nm PCIe Gen 6 tape-out August 2026; >12 Tier 1 customers awaiting samples; initial share target 15-20%; growth driver in 2028

Ferri for Automotive and Enterprise Boot Drive solutions MORE THAN DOUBLED sequentially and now represent nearly 30% of total revenue, up from 4% a year ago. These are controller-plus-NAND solutions, so ASPs are much higher than controller-only (and higher than MonTitan). The DRAM-less boot drive is the crown jewel: conventional DRAM-based boot drives for server CPUs stay with the NAND makers, but DPUs, TPUs, NPUs and switches favour DRAM-less designs for cost, security and performance - and NAND makers have no DRAM-less PCIe SSD controllers and little incentive to build them for a market where densities are only 256GB-512GB. A server rack can carry more than 30 or 40 boot drives, and per-drive capacity should rise. Management sees little competition from either NAND makers or module makers, and said Ferri plus Boot Drive reaching roughly one third of revenue in 2027 is 'certainly a possibility' given current backlog and pipeline.
Ferri + Boot Drive more than doubled QoQ to ~30% of revenue (from 4% a year ago); >30-40 boot drives per server rack

Edge SSD controllers grew 40-45% year over year in Q2 after a seasonally soft Q1, and SSD revenue is up about 50% versus the first half of last year on share gains despite declining PC units. The PCIe 4 to PCIe 5 transition is proceeding MORE SLOWLY than management expected six months ago: OEMs are pairing the latest, more cost-effective NAND with PCIe 4 SSDs in value and mainstream PCs to cut bill-of-materials cost. The 4-channel PCIe 5 controller introduced in Q4 of last year continues to ramp steadily in the mid- to high-end PC segment, and management still expects SSD average selling prices to rise through the year.
Edge SSD +40-45% YoY; SSD revenue ~+50% vs prior-year first half; PCIe 4-to-5 transition slower than expected

→ NVIDIA: Asked whether BlueField-4 was contributing as NVIDIA ramps the Vera Rubin platform, CEO Wallace Kou said Silicon Motion has 'a pretty large share for BlueField supply for Boot Drives' and expects to benefit as BlueField ramps in the second half of 2026, declining to comment on generation timing beyond the customer's own announcements. Boot Drive wins extend beyond DPUs to TPUs, telco customers and leading server makers, and management said the business 'could grow even more strongly next year' with the leading GPU company.

RECORD MEMORY-TEST QUARTER: Teradyne posted a second consecutive record quarter (revenue $1,329M, above the high end of guidance) with 'RECORD MEMORY REVENUE driven by continued strength in DRAM and A RESURGENCE IN NAND FINAL TEST' — the NAND-test recovery arriving on cue with the NAND upgrade cycle other chain members flagged. Semiconductor Test revenue $1,122M of the $1,329M total; GAAP EPS $2.38. Q3 2026 guided to $1,200-1,300M with non-GAAP EPS $1.85-2.15, reflecting 'robust AI-related demand'; CEO Greg Smith: 'rapid increase in WAFER FAB EQUIPMENT investment sets the stage for continued growth in 2027 and beyond.'
Record memory revenue (DRAM strength + NAND final-test resurgence); Q2 rev $1,329M record

CALL — MEMORY TEST: BOOK-TO-BILL OVER 2 AND A +40% TAM: memory revenue hit a third straight >$200M record ($212M) with the quarter's memory BOOK-TO-BILL RATIO OVER 2 as 'memory manufacturers are planning capacity additions further out in time'; the 2026 MEMORY TEST TAM is likely MORE THAN 40% LARGER THAN 2025, growing H1->H2. Drivers re-ranked: HBM strength was expected, but the SURPRISE is DDR — 'coupled to the resurgence in CPU-oriented applications, so AGENTIC AI' plus LPDDR inside SoCs; and the long-awaited NAND INFLECTION IS NOW REAL ('we actually have seen the beginning... getting PULL from our customers for more NAND capacity'). HBM die test a highlight — Magnum's logic-test capability gives memory makers a SWING-TOOL advantage between memory and logic test. 2027: NO lumpiness expected — WFE investment, new fabs and wafer-output plans have customers making test-capacity plans INTO 2027 already; memory TAM has two flywheels (bit growth ~15-20% CAGR + technology transitions HBM3->4, DDR5->6, flash generations); memory remains a GROSS-MARGIN strain into 2027 (SoC TAM still ~5x the memory TAM). Teradyne expects to GAIN memory-test share (Advantest publicly concurs it is losing some).
Memory b2b >2; 2026 memory-test TAM +>40%; DDR the surprise (agentic-AI CPU pull); NAND inflection real; share shifting to Teradyne

SECOND CONSECUTIVE RECORD QUARTER, above the high end of guidance: revenue $1,329M — Semiconductor Test $1,122M, Product Test $107M, Robotics $100M — with GAAP net income $374.5M and GAAP EPS $2.38 (non-GAAP net income $389M). Year-on-year market expansion across ALL THREE business groups; record MEMORY revenue on DRAM strength plus a NAND final-test resurgence. CEO Greg Smith frames the arc: 'our strategy to capture test and robotics opportunities FROM WAFER TO AI DATA CENTER has driven another record quarter... In the short term, our Q3 guidance reflects robust AI-related demand. Looking further ahead, RAPID INCREASE IN WAFER FAB EQUIPMENT INVESTMENT sets the stage for continued growth in 2027 and beyond.' Q3 2026 guide: revenue $1,200-1,300M, non-GAAP EPS $1.85-2.15.
Record $1,329M (Semi Test $1,122M); record memory test; WFE surge = 2027+ growth setup

CALL — HBM PROCESS-CONTROL INTENSITY 'RIVALS ADVANCED LOGIC': CFO Bren Higgins said HBM is 'a unique animal' for KLA — base-die CUSTOMIZATION, the integration of each DRAM in the stack, the ultimate device value and tighter performance specs are driving process-control intensity levels 'RIVALING WHAT WE SEE IN ADVANCED LOGIC' across some products; conventional DRAM intensity has improved but is NOT the same as HBM. 2027 memory setup: DRAM investment broad across conventional AND HBM with GREENFIELD FABS (whole new toolsets, not just upgrades) — 'given where prices are and how that translates into margins, the VALUE OF YIELD is pretty high,' plus rising EUV adoption in DRAM; even NAND gets some greenfield. Mix: September quarter memory = 27% of semi-PC systems (DRAM 90% / NAND 10%); memory share RISES in the December quarter and stays elevated through H1 2027. Cost side: the memory-pricing gross-margin headwind is ~100bps 'and probably a little bit more' and now expected to CONTINUE THROUGH 2027 (new memory procured at higher prices) before normalizing into a TAILWIND.
HBM PC intensity rivals advanced logic; DRAM greenfield + EUV in 2027; memory GM headwind ~100bps+ through 2027 then tailwind

Memory market: AI servers keep driving HBM demand and high-end memory packaging demand stays very strong; DRAM and NAND market demand and prices are rising together, with customers maximising output of committed capacity - customer revenue gains are mostly price-driven as supply is limited, but PTI's packaging volumes are still growing and utilisation keeps improving. Packaging material costs keep rising and PTI is passing them through to customers gradually (its customers are large long-term partners, so price adjustments are made carefully each quarter). AI-server eSSD demand keeps rising with shipments expanding QoQ and YoY.

WFE is expected to grow about 20% in calendar 2026 and a similar level in calendar 2027. Updated CY2026 growth by application: advanced logic foundry over 20%, DRAM over 25% (raised), NAND about 20% (raised from a bit less than 15%), power devices a bit less than 10%. Foundry AI-driven leading edge investment is the primary WFE driver; advanced DRAM and HBM are in shortage and even existing DDR is in shortage, so CapEx is going into both HBM and general DDR, with strong NAND investment also expected as data center demand recovers. Memory device makers are asking for accelerated delivery - demand is now stronger than SCREEN's current capacity. Average equipment lead time is about 4.2 months. Chinese demand for advanced AI-related tools is at record-high inquiry levels.
WFE about 20% growth in calendar 2026 and 2027; DRAM over 25%, NAND about 20%, advanced logic foundry over 20%; lead time 4.2 months; demand stronger than capacity

CALL-ONLY / DEMAND-SIDE READ ON THE MEMORY SHORTAGE: at the OSAT level the DRAM squeeze is now measurable in handset volumes - Amkor's ANDROID revenue fell 20% SEQUENTIALLY 'reflecting the impact of MEMORY SUPPLY DYNAMICS', and Q3 communications is guided down high-single-digits sequentially (against normal seasonality) partly on 'ongoing MEMORY SUPPLY CONSTRAINTS', with memory PRICING also expected to weigh on phone unit volumes this year. Capacity response: Amkor's phased Vietnam build-out is adding SiP and NAND MEMORY capacity, while Korea's freed floor space is redirected to computing/advanced-packaging programs.
Android -20% QoQ on memory supply; Vietnam adding SiP + NAND memory capacity

CALL-ONLY: ARIZONA PHASE I IS NOW FULLY COMMITTED - 'our projections now show phase I as fully committed', with future expansion phases under evaluation. Global build-out detail given on the call: KOREA - the new Songdo assembly & test building remains on schedule for completion by end-2026, and the GWANGJU campus expansion adds clean-room capacity for data-center and advanced-packaging growth 'in 2028 AND BEYOND'; VIETNAM, PORTUGAL and TAIWAN are taking incremental clean room and equipment installs; Vietnam is being built out in phases for SiP and NAND MEMORY capacity, and moving SiP out of Korea 'enables additional capacity for our rapidly scaling COMPUTING programs in Korea'. 2026 capex reaffirmed at $2.5-3.0B: 65-70% facilities expansion (including Arizona Phase I), 30-35% HDFO/test/other advanced packaging, remainder R&D and quality. The cost of that build is explicit: ramping, UNDERUTILIZED Arizona manufacturing will be a drag on BOTH gross margin and operating margin in 2028 - the reason the 2028 target model looks similar to 2026 despite the growth.
Arizona Phase I FULLY COMMITTED; capex $2.5-3.0B (65-70% facilities); Gwangju cleanroom for 2028+

Build-out (five largest sites): ABILENE TX 42% of capacity delivered, +35% more within 90 days, remainder the following quarter; SHACKLEFORD TX delivery 1H CY27 with 115MW power online >1 month early; DONA ANA COUNTY NM delivery 1H CY27 — design based on GIGAWATTS of clean BLOOM fuel cells; SALINE MI delivery 2H 2027 (network core ahead of schedule, end of CY26); PORT WASHINGTON WI delivery 2H CY27. Funding: FY27 net cash capex ~$70B EXCLUDING $20-25B of customer PREPAYMENTS (reported capex higher); ~$40B debt+equity raise in FY27 incl. the $20B ATM equity program; no additional debt in CY2026. Component-cost protection: fixed-price customer contracts ONLY when costs are locked — otherwise FLOATING-cost mechanisms pass through memory/SSD/HDD inflation.
5 mega-sites ramping (Abilene 42%+35%/90d); FY27 capex ~$70B net; floating-cost contracts shield margins

Record Q2 FY2026 revenue $10.7B (+40% YoY, +15% QoQ), non-GAAP EPS $0.79 (+108% YoY), free cash flow $915M, gross margin 36.9%, operating margin 13.3%. Orders more than doubled, far outpacing revenue, for a record company backlog. Raised FY2026 outlook to ~$3.40 non-GAAP EPS (+40%) and at least $3.5B FCF — two years ahead of the long-term plan. Cloud & AI segment revenue $7.7B (+23%); traditional server orders grew triple-digits on agentic-AI inferencing; DRAM/NAND inflation + supply constraints lifting server ASPs (working with silicon/memory partners on long-term supply).

Sequential revenue +15% reflects higher server ASPs from DRAM/NAND inflationary costs; networking products constrained by DDR4/DDR5 and wafer capacity ('supply chain is the name of the game in networking' — purchase commitments +40% sequentially). FY2026 guide assumes NO incremental supply; component costs expected elevated into 2027 until new fabs yield. Inferencing accelerating as a demand driver — 'a lot of these inferencing deployments will be done on CPUs', traditional-server orders up triple digits on agentic-AI/high-memory configs; by end of decade Neri expects MOST demand to be inferencing. FY2027 framework: revenue +8-12% with AI-systems revenue accelerating.
DRAM/NAND-driven ASPs; no incremental 2026 supply; FY27 +8-12%

Data-center optics ramp: on the receiver side both 100G and 200G products are in mass production and shipping, with 100G (i.e. 800G transceivers) the mainstay this year and 1.6T expected to be a breakout next year. On the transmit side, 400G lasers entered mass production in Q2 2026 (first design win back in March 2023), with volumes expected to multiply next year, and CW laser customers have been in mass production since Q4 2024. New applications: solar-cell substrates for drones and low-earth-orbit satellites (including radiation-resistant flexible solar panels, with an LEO satellite project this year), and VCSELs used as the heating source in HAMR HDDs - in development for two years, with a meaningful contribution expected next year and the year after.

receiver-side 100G and 200G in mass production; 800G the mainstay this year with a 1.6T breakout expected next year; transmit-side 400G in mass production from Q2; CW lasers in production since Q4 2024

Four AI pillars: (1) AI infrastructure scaling — clusters integrating GPUs/CPUs/DPUs/switches/NICs/memory fabrics across vendors (Ethernet, UALink, PCIe, NVMe) incl. rack-backplane characterization for next-gen scale-up networks; (2) SPEED TRANSITIONS — 800G deployments accelerating 1.6T adoption with rising 3.2T R&D; (3) optical/photonics technologies; (4) system-level emulation. At OFC Keysight demonstrated 1.6T physical-layer solutions with 20+ industry leaders (traffic emulation, link reliability, SerDes signal integrity) and ran the industry's FIRST public Ultra Ethernet Consortium interoperability demo WITH BROADCOM.
1.6T test w/ 20+ leaders at OFC; first UEC interop demo w/ Broadcom; 3.2T R&D rising

Product/strategy: HBM TC bonders (12/16-high stacking) remain the core. KEY DISCLOSURE: because the industry's HYBRID-BONDER development is DELAYED by technical hurdles, 20-high+ HBM stacking needs a new tool that can bond WIDER dies — Hanmi is about to launch the "WIDE TC BONDER" for next-gen HBM structures, while ALSO developing hybrid bonders (for HBM and for system-semiconductor stacking) in parallel. Portfolio extensions: 6-SIDE INSPECTION (pre/post-TC-bond HBM yield control), world-first two-in-one BOC+COB bonder (stacked GDDR, enterprise eSSD), entry into 2.5D PACKAGING (TC/FC/die bonders for interposer integration of HBM + base die + CPU/GPU), MSVP 8.0 saw/vision placement (world #1 since mid-2000s, boosted by larger PLP/chiplet panels), EMI Shield 2.0 X (#1 share). Disclosed customer list: SK Hynix, MICRON, ASE, Amkor, JCET, Huatian, TFME, Infineon, STMicro, PTI, Skyworks, Luxshare + Korean OSATs/Samsung Electro-Mechanics/LG Innotek.
WIDE TC bonder launch imminent (hybrid-bonder delay = TC extension); 2.5D packaging entry; Micron now a disclosed customer

Product positioning: CUBE PROBER — full inspection of HBM at the individual-stack level with precision vision (filing: AI-driven HBM demand surging; HBM market led by SK Hynix/Samsung/Micron) — plus TWP300/TWP300H probe stations targeting localization of a market dominated by Tokyo Electron, and expansion from memory test handlers into SoC handlers, SSD/burn-in/wafer test solutions.
Cube Prober = per-stack HBM full-inspection; probe-station localization vs TEL
SUMCO projects an uptick in NAND wafer demand ahead as part of robust overall 300mm demand driven by AI data centers (Q1 2026 view).

Wafer market outlook: semiconductor market sees continued strong AI growth and only gradual recovery elsewhere. 300mm demand strong for leading-edge logic and DRAM in AI data centers with a projected NAND uptick ahead; recovery in non-leading-edge logic is gradual and partly TEMPERED BY MEMORY SHORTAGES (memory supply constraints curb non-leading-edge logic demand). 200mm and smaller lacks momentum, inventory-adjustment progress varies by customer.
AI leading-edge strong vs non-AI gradual; memory shortage caps non-leading-edge logic

MARKET / ROADMAP DATA POINTS: 800G transceiver INDUSTRY volume went from ~20 MILLION UNITS/YEAR two years ago to ~90 MILLION UNITS/YEAR this year — the industry entered the year forecasting 50M units and Semtech is 'now hearing the number 80, 90 million'; 800G bookings are still INCREASING (not decreasing), and 800G and 1.6T both have 'a really very healthy runway over the next two years'. 3.2T TIMING: design window starts opening in ~12 MONTHS, EARLY MOVERS ~18 MONTHS OUT, MEANINGFUL DEPLOYMENT IN ~2 YEARS (i.e. H2 CY2028) — that is the cut-in for Semtech's content step-up, and above 200G/lane is where TIA + photodiode CO-OPTIMIZATION becomes necessary. MPO/NPO called a strong trend driven by BANDWIDTH-DENSITY limits against fixed shoreline: Semtech is engaged on '10, 15 DIFFERENT PROGRAMS' with module manufacturers, some tied directly to end customers, as a leading supplier of TIA ARRAYS and (linearized) LASER ARRAYS; higher density tightens element spacing and crosstalk, changing packaging requirements. LPO has generated meaningful revenue since Q1 FY2027 and is growing moderately, but its bigger effect is PROVING THE LINEAR ARCHITECTURE, which now carries into MPO, XPO and 'some form of CPO'. Stated R&D priority: lasers, photodiodes, drivers and TIAs for 3.2T coherent light, XPO, MPO and CPO applications. Analyst day 10-15-2026 (San Jose) will publish TAM, share and the multi-year model.
800G industry units ~20M/yr (2024) → ~90M/yr (2026); 3.2T volume ~2 years out; 10-15 MPO/NPO programs

ADI's optical franchise targets the CONTROL PATH, not the electro-optic data path: 'there are two critical pathways, the data path of electro optics and the control path, which guides, optimizes, and ensures the integrity of the data path. Our focus is on the control path.' Customers increasingly rely on ADI for the timing, power management, data conversion, monitoring and control that let LASERS AND TRANSCEIVERS operate with precision, reliably and efficiently at AI scale. Data center optical revenue grew MORE THAN 100% year-over-year in fiscal Q3 2026 (data center is now 80% of ADI communications revenue, which itself was +84% YoY).
Data center optical revenue +100%+ YoY; control-path timing/power/conversion for lasers & transceivers

800G -> 3.2T TRANSITION: as customers increase the number of optical lanes, signal bandwidth, or both, to accelerate network speeds from 800 Gb to 3.2 Tbps, ADI expects to benefit THREEFOLD - unit growth in pluggables and coherent light modules, INCREASING BOM CONTENT per module, and GREATER SHARE as these transitions unfold.

Segment detail: communications was 16% of revenue, +18% sequentially and +84% year-over-year. DATA CENTER now accounts for 80% of communications revenue (up from >75% last quarter) and grew MORE THAN 100% year-over-year in BOTH optical AND power. Wireless +25% YoY. Industrial 49% of revenue (+10% QoQ, +53% YoY) led by ATE, electronic test & measurement, aerospace/defense and automation; automotive 25% (+14% QoQ, +16% YoY) on next-gen ADAS, infotainment and electric powertrains; consumer 10% (flat QoQ, +6% YoY) despite memory-driven challenges.
Comms +84% YoY (80% data center); data center optical AND power each +100%+ YoY

Market position and mix shift: the company estimates its Q2 2026 global CCL share at 30% in package CCL, 22% in flexible CCL (single and double sided) and 16% in halogen-free CCL. The sales strategy has moved away from commodity grades toward high-function products, specifically NWB CCL for AI accelerators and data centers, PKG CCL for semiconductors and halogen-free CCL for optical modules, sold into the global market, and 2026 targets a higher weighting of high-value products together with supply diversification to global customers beyond Samsung. The unit says CCL requires prior quality and specification approval from both the set maker and the PCB maker before it can be used, and that the industry is led by roughly ten suppliers from Korea, China, Taiwan and Japan.
Estimated global share Q2 2026: package CCL 30%, flexible CCL 22%, halogen-free CCL 16%

SCALE-ACROSS is the emerging motion: Cisco estimates network traffic generated by AI-based scale-across is roughly 14x what traditional data-center interconnect produced. Three new hyperscaler design wins in Q4 — (1) a Silicon One P200-powered system for SCALE-ACROSS, the third P200 scale-across win since launch, EACH WITH A SEPARATE HYPERSCALER, with orders already received from all three in Q4; (2) a G200-powered system for scale-out; and (3) a MANAGED OPTICAL FIBER NETWORK win using Cisco's line-system technology that enables its digital coherent optics inside THIRD-PARTY equipment — strategically positioning Cisco as an alternative to an incumbent competitor. Cisco has line of sight to multiple further AI design wins over the next six months across G300, G200 and P200 silicon plus optics, and MULTI-RAIL OPTICAL SYSTEMS are 'coming soon' / beginning to deploy. Acacia took over $1B of orders in Q4 and has now shipped over 850,000 400G and over 75,000 800G coherent pluggables to date (versus >750,000 and >40,000 at Q3).
scale-across traffic ~14x DCI; 3rd P200 scale-across win (3 separate hyperscalers, all ordering); Acacia >850k 400G / >75k 800G shipped

Record Q4 revenue $2.05B (+42% YoY pro forma) with data center revenue +66% YoY; FY2026 revenue $7.12B (+28% pro forma) and non-GAAP EPS $5.61 (+59%). Coherent targets its first quarter above $3B of revenue by the end of fiscal 2027. Bookings hit another record: fiscal 2027 is basically completely booked out, backlog runs through the end of calendar 2027, customers are now placing orders into calendar 2028, and LTAs extend through the end of the decade with take-or-pay minimum demand guarantees. Both 800G and 1.6T grow through calendar 2026; indium phosphide capacity remains the primary supply constraint, doubling YoY by the end of the September quarter.
Q4 $2.05B, DC +66% YoY; FY27 booked out, orders into CY2028, LTAs to end of decade

800G is NOT rolling over as 1.6T ramps — Coherent expects 800G revenue to CONTINUE GROWING YEAR-OVER-YEAR through calendar 2026 alongside the rapid 1.6T ramp. Q4 data center revenue +24% QoQ and +66% YoY. Indium phosphide is the binding constraint across the portfolio (assembly and test capacity is available); June-quarter InP laser output — the lasers that feed both 800G and 1.6T transceivers — was up about 80% YoY, and internal InP capacity doubles YoY by the end of the September quarter, one quarter ahead of plan.
800G still growing YoY through CY2026; InP laser output +80% YoY; InP is the constraint

Both transceiver tiers grow together: 800G revenue continues rising year-over-year through calendar 2026 while 1.6T ramps rapidly into 2027 as adoption broadens. Q4 data center revenue +24% QoQ, +66% YoY, the third consecutive quarter of double-digit sequential growth. Supply, not demand, is the limiter — indium phosphide capacity is the primary constraint (assembly and test have headroom), with internal InP output doubling YoY by the end of the September quarter and more than doubling again by end of calendar 2027.
800G + 1.6T both growing; DC revenue +66% YoY; InP the primary constraint

OCS addressable market held at MORE THAN $4 BILLION (doubled from $2B at OFC 2026, 2030 timeframe) and management suggests even that may be conservative — applications have widened from the original scale-out focus to scale-across and now a clear path to SCALE-UP, where there are active customer engagements. OCS revenue grew sequentially in Q4 and is expected to grow significantly through fiscal 2027 as production expands across two manufacturing locations, spanning the 320x320 platform and other system sizes. 1.6T transceivers are ramping rapidly through calendar 2026 into 2027, with the ramp pulled in versus the prior quarter's assumptions.
OCS TAM >$4B and widening to scale-up; OCS revenue growing across two plants; 1.6T ramp pulled in

Segment detail. DATA CENTER AND COMMUNICATIONS segment +40% for FY2026; Q4 +19% QoQ and +59% YoY. DATA CENTER business +41% FY2026; Q4 +24% QoQ and +66% YoY — a third consecutive quarter of double-digit sequential growth, with strong sequential growth expected again in Q1. COMMUNICATIONS +54% FY2026; Q4 +11% QoQ and +56% YoY on data-center interconnect, scale-across and traditional telecom, with particular strength in ZR/ZR+ DCI transceivers, pump lasers and complex high-end optical subsystems. INDUSTRIAL was roughly flat pro forma in both FY2026 and Q4 — semiconductor and display capital equipment grew but were offset by broader industrial weakness; growth is expected to resume led by semicap, where bookings continue to strengthen. Within transceivers, 800G revenue keeps growing YoY through calendar 2026 while 1.6T ramps rapidly through the balance of 2026 into 2027, with the 1.6T ramp PULLED IN and stronger than management assumed three months ago.
Q4 data center +66% YoY, comms +56% YoY; 1.6T ramp pulled in vs 3 months ago

INDIUM PHOSPHIDE IS THE PRIMARY CONSTRAINT on the whole business — 'we're not constrained in assembly and test capacity right now... we're really just constrained by the ramp of the indium phosphide production.' Internal InP output capacity doubles YoY by the end of the current quarter, ONE QUARTER AHEAD of the original plan, and is on track to MORE THAN DOUBLE AGAIN by the end of calendar 2027; substrates and other critical inputs for that ramp are already secured, and capacity beyond 2027 is being planned. Concrete measure: Coherent produced about 80% MORE indium phosphide lasers in the June quarter than a year earlier — those lasers feed 800G and 1.6T transceiver shipments in the current quarter, so management expects data-center revenue growth this quarter to EXCEED 80% YoY. Six-inch lines in TEXAS and SWEDEN are producing EMLs, CW lasers and photodiodes with yields that exceed the 3-inch lines across all three device types; a third 6-inch location in ZURICH starts in the first half of calendar 2027. Six-inch economics: 4x the output per wafer at half the cost.
InP output 2x YoY (a quarter early), 2x again by end-CY2027; June-qtr lasers +80% YoY; 6-inch = 4x output at half the cost

H1 networking-product revenue grew strongly on higher switch volumes and rising ASPs as AI racks push network bandwidth and interconnect needs. The target of roughly doubling 800G-and-above switch revenue this year is unchanged, and CPO optical switches are on plan for volume production and shipment in Q3 - CPO switches have already begun shipping, currently used mainly for scale-out links between AI racks and later extending as platform generations and system architecture upgrade. Foxconn is also building out optical modules, optoelectronic integration, advanced packaging, cables/connectors and high-speed transmission and power-management modules to lift in-house content; it sees optical communications and networking as the next major AI-infrastructure growth leg, with a market that could exceed US$100 billion, and its research institute announced an ultra-high-capacity silicon photonics technology for supercomputing transmission.
800G+ switch revenue on track to double in 2026; CPO switch volume production and shipment from Q3

EMLs delivered another record-breaking quarter, primarily driven by 100G-per-lane devices. 200G EMLs are accelerating and now account for over 25% of total EML revenue; management expects 200G EMLs to be 50% or more of volume by mid-calendar-2027. Lumentum remains on track to deliver over 50% EML unit growth in the December 2026 quarter versus the year-ago quarter, but expects to remain significantly behind demand even at year end.
record EML quarter; 200G EML >25% of EML revenue; >50% EML unit growth by Dec-2026 quarter

Capacity: expanding across the two indium phosphide wafer fabs in Japan to capture coming 200G and 300G lane-speed opportunities, qualifying both CW and EML process flows on the newest tools as they come online. Demand for both EML and CW lasers is expected to grow significantly through the second half of calendar 2026 and into 2027.
two Japan InP fabs expanding; CW and EML flows qualifying on new tools

Cloud transceivers: record 800G shipments in the quarter while initiating production of next-generation 1.6T modules. Transceiver profitability continues to improve on yield gains, capacity utilization, and the initial rollout of higher-ASP 1.6T units. 1.6T uptake is expected to intensify starting in fiscal Q1 FY2027 and sustain through calendar 2027, anchored by lead Tier 1 hyperscale customers rolling out custom AI clusters. Management believes Lumentum is first to market ahead of larger competitors in many instances and can hold that share advantage through the cycle, crediting its signal integrity team on difficult 1.6T designs.
record 800G shipments; 1.6T production initiated; 1.6T uptake intensifies from fiscal Q1 FY2027

Technology roadmap view: silicon photonics is a viable solution at 1.6T and CW lasers are taking a significant portion of transceiver output, but at 3.2T silicon photonics 'loses some of its advantages' and Lumentum expects EMLs to come back in a meaningful way. Wupen Yuen added that in a supply-constrained environment customers will use whichever laser source they can get, so the EML-versus-CW mix is a supply/demand dynamic as much as a technical one. CPO remains the natural end state - optics placed directly on the substrate or interposer for maximum power efficiency through foundry-level advanced packaging.
SiPho viable at 1.6T; EML expected to return at 3.2T; CPO the end state via foundry advanced packaging

Networking is now an explicit DCBBS pillar: the total solution spans CPU and GPU compute, storage, energy and a 1.6T HIGH-SPEED SWITCH plus 'upcoming optical networking', sold with the Supermicro management software suite (SCM, SuperCloud Composer, SVM, SOM). The new 32-acre Silicon Valley DCBBS campus features an ADVANCED OPTICAL PHOTONICS NETWORKING LAB alongside datacenter-scale manufacturing, and management calls out high-speed switch and optical technology as areas of very aggressive continued investment, with the 'high bandwidth switch and the whole networking design management tool' cited as a big room to grow toward the ~20%-of-gross-profit DCBBS target. Customer networking readiness (alongside power and cooling) was one of the causes of the Q4 revenue push-out.
1.6T switch shipping in DCBBS; optical networking upcoming; SV photonics lab

1.6T optical-module PCB: current orders are mainly 1.6T high-speed optical-module boards; 2026 optical-module related revenue is guided to double, 1.6T keeps growing sharply in 2027 and becomes the main shipping spec in 2028, and 3.2T boards are already being sampled. Customers are already pre-booking 2027 capacity; target is to become the world's largest high-end optical-module PCB supplier in 2027. 800G-and-above optical-module boards require M7-class ultra-low-loss laminate (1.6T effectively mandates it); management says roughly 20 players claim to be entering optical modules but few master M7 high-layer board production, which is why Zhen Ding's substrate-derived M7 technology gave it the 1.6T breakout. 1.6T optical-module board yield is described as industry-leading at above 90%, including the newly ramped Thailand lines. On a potential US FCC ban on Chinese optical modules: Zhen Ding supplies the PCB inside the module, not the module itself, so sees no direct hit, and can shift production to Thailand where customers require it. On CPO: the company says it will participate in both pluggable and CPO/NPO architectures as they develop; most PCB equipment is transferable between product types so a CPO shift would strand little capacity.
2026 optical-module revenue to double; 1.6T main spec by 2028; 3.2T sampling; 1.6T board yield above 90%; goal: largest high-end optical-module PCB supplier in 2027

Data center revenue $107.7M, +140.4% Y/Y and +32.3% Q/Q. SPEED MIX of data center revenue: 100G 38.3% (+31.3% Y/Y), 200G/400G 45% ($48.4M, >4x Y/Y, +27.4% Q/Q), 800G 11.9% ($12.8M, >10x Y/Y, MORE THAN DOUBLED sequentially), 10G/40G 4.4%. 800G revenue is guided to grow NEARLY 5x SEQUENTIALLY in Q3, with continued strong Q4 growth gated by production capacity and component supply.

1.6T RAMP BEGINS: full qualification of AOI's first 1.6T product at the hyperscale customer expected 'within the next couple of weeks', with 1.6T shipments starting later in Q3 - AOI says it will be the FOURTH supplier qualified at that one big hyperscale data center customer for 1.6T. The customer returns to 10%+ of revenue in Q3. The previously announced order is now sized at MORE THAN $200M in hand: deliveries start very late Q3, the BULK ships in Q4, with a tail into Q1 2027 (target to complete by ~Q2 2027) - and management frames it as 'just the very beginning' of significant recurring 1.6T orders. Q4 1.6T revenue commitment $70-80M (limited by MATERIAL supply, not capacity); Q1 2027 1.6T revenue targeted to DOUBLE Q4 or more. Q4 combined 800G+1.6T revenue of ~$330M confirmed 'about right, directionally'. Longer term, customer feedback points to >500,000 1.6T transceivers/month by end-2027 = $300-350M/month.
>$200M 1.6T orders in hand; Q4 1.6T $70-80M; Q4 800G+1.6T ~$330M; >500k units/mo ($300-350M/mo) by end-2027

MID-2027 MONTHLY RUN-RATE TARGET REITERATED: by mid-2027 management expects ~$90M/month from 100G+400G, ~$217M/month from 800G and ~$164M/month from 1.6T = ABOUT $471M PER MONTH of data center transceiver revenue. Near-term bridge: Q3 revenue guided to $255-290M (+130% Y/Y at midpoint) and Q4 'more than $500 million' (~60% Q/Q growth) as capacity comes online.
~$471M/month DC transceiver revenue by mid-2027 (800G $217M + 1.6T $164M + 100/400G $90M); Q4 2026 >$500M

CAPACITY RAMP: 800G/1.6T manufacturing capacity is 'approaching 200,000 units per month' now, up from ~100,000/month exiting Q1 FY2026; expected to reach OVER 650,000 pieces/month by END-2026 and OVER 930,000 pieces/month by END-2027, with MORE THAN HALF of that output from TEXAS. Texas footprint expanded to OVER 1.6 MILLION sq ft in greater Houston (vs ~900k sq ft reported at Q1 FY2026 and only ~65,000 sq ft a year ago). The 210k sq ft facility (dedicated 800G/1.6T) starts initial production LATE in Q3; moving transceiver lines out of headquarters frees that fab to expand INDIUM PHOSPHIDE wafer capacity; Pearland (construction started) and Houston buildouts come online EARLY 2027. Capacity is 'complete book already from now until Q2 next year' and customer demand runs 20-40% ABOVE planned capacity. 800G and 1.6T run on the SAME line and process (1.6T differs only in final test), so 800G->1.6T scaling needs minimal incremental investment.
~200k units/mo now -> >650k/mo end-2026 -> >930k/mo end-2027 (>50% from Texas); TX footprint >1.6M sqft; booked through Q2 2027

CPO / ELSFP EXTERNAL LASER SOURCE ECONOMICS: ELSFP (external light source for co-packaged optics) is in very limited production now, ramping later in 2026 and through 2027 to ~400,000 PIECES PER MONTH IN 2028. Laser power scaling is the constraint: CPO/ELSFP uses a 300mW laser vs 70mW in an 800G transceiver and 100mW in a 1.6T transceiver, with die size ~6x larger, so meeting CPO demand requires the industry laser market to be 8-10x BIGGER than today; the next generation of ELSFP moves to DWDM, where yield loss is 40-50% worse than 1310nm. Laser capacity carries a 21-24 MONTH equipment-to-high-volume lead time. AOI is engaged with ~5 CPO customers on 3-4 year demand; several have already qualified AOI on fixed-wavelength CPO laser / ELSFP, with DWDM the current focus. High-volume ELSFP manufacturing is 'more like late Q3 next year' (late 2027). Houston laser fab capacity to grow ~300% by Q3 2027 plus a SECOND FAB cleanroom ~4x the size of the current facility (adding MOCVD, epi, steppers). Margin mix: laser gross margin 55-65%, ELSFP module ('EOSAP') >50%, both landing H2 2027. AOI is absent from first-generation CPO deployments purely because laser capacity must first feed AOI's own transceivers.
ELSFP ~400k pcs/month in 2028; 300mW CPO laser vs 70mW(800G)/100mW(1.6T); industry laser capacity needs 8-10x; laser GM 55-65%

BOTTLENECK HAS MOVED FROM LASERS TO DSP/TIA: because AOI makes its own lasers in-house it avoids the laser shortage that management calls 'the biggest bottleneck right now for the transceiver business' and 'the number one issue' for competitors; AOI's binding constraints for 800G/1.6T are instead DSP and TIA supply, where 'the whole supply chain is very tight' for 1.6T - AOI says its supplier ranks it FOURTH priority under a long-term partnership, with calls once or twice a week. INDIUM PHOSPHIDE SUBSTRATE: supply secured into end-2027 and 'incrementally better' than last quarter - not currently a limiter; AOI has just moved to 4-INCH substrate volume manufacturing and buys from 2 European + 2 Japanese + 3 Chinese suppliers, and is negotiating partnerships or a possible JOINT VENTURE with 2-3 of them for 2028-2029 volumes (laser capacity growing 'much more than a factor of 10'). Proprietary in-house production machinery insulates AOI from the industry's equipment-delivery bottlenecks.
DSP/TIA = binding constraint (AOI ranked 4th priority); InP substrate secured to end-2027; 4-inch substrate volume production

Data Center revenue was a record $137.6 million, up approximately 40% sequentially, driven by 800G and 1.6T PAM4 demand. The segment grew 35% in 2024 and 48% in 2025 and is trending toward about 74% THIS YEAR. The primary driver from fiscal 2025 to 2026 is 200-gig PAM4 products in pluggable optical modules; ZR and ZR-light are growing over 100% year over year; 100-gig-per-lane single mode and multimode are posting high double-digit growth; and legacy 25-gig-per-lane products for 100G FR and LR4 are also growing strongly. Book-to-bill within Data Center is driven primarily by 1.6T and 800G platforms. MACOM is sampling its latest generation 200G and 400G PER LANE TIAs and drivers. A structural tailwind: hyperscalers are moving from PASSIVE COPPER TO FIBER in scale-up applications, which is pure SAM expansion for MACOM because it does not promote passive copper solutions.
Data Center revenue $137.6M (+~40% QoQ, record); segment growth 35% in 2024, 48% in 2025, ~74% trending this year

NPO and XPO positioning: MACOM has BETWEEN 10 AND 20 ACTIVE NPO DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS across various customers and use cases, and expects some of that revenue to kick in IN 2028, with NPO starting to grow significantly from 2028. Critically, MACOM says it will NOT build or supply optical engines - in Data Center it is a chip supplier, not a multichip assembly or module supplier. It describes the architectural evolution as pluggable transceivers with DSPs, to LPO platforms that remove the DSP, morphing into smaller package-less NPO platforms; those architectures still need drivers and TIAs, but with much higher density - smaller parts, more channels, lower power, and varied form factors using wire bonds, bumped devices or flip chip, plus through-silicon-via options. Because these solutions are specific to the architectures hyperscalers are driving, the design wins come directly to MACOM. Related applications include LPO and LRO on single mode or multimode.
10-20 active NPO development projects; NPO revenue expected to begin in 2028

Indium phosphide is the key medium-term lever. 200-GIG PHOTODETECTORS are ramping in volume production and becoming a meaningful contributor to Data Center growth; 400-gig photodetectors are in the hands of perhaps a dozen customers with very positive feedback. The 75-MILLIWATT CW LASER qualification continues: MACOM is well into HTOL testing (typically 5,000 hours) with data described as exceptional, is gaining confidence but cannot yet declare success, and is developing plans for a POTENTIAL START TO PRODUCTION IN LATE CALENDAR 2027, scoping modest capex and fab space for a rapid high-volume ramp for a few strategic customers. CEO Steve Daly called bringing a CW laser into production in 2028 'a watershed moment' that could be a very large revenue contributor. Separately, demand for MACOM's 25G DFB lasers (100G QSFP, CWDM4, LR4) is rising with urgency because of a GENERAL SUPPLY SHORTAGE OF INDIUM PHOSPHIDE DFB LASERS. MACOM expects to gain meaningful indium phosphide market share over the next three years; its Ann Arbor, Michigan facility has built photodiodes for over a decade and grows its own epitaxy by MBE.
200G PDs ramping in volume; 400G PDs at ~a dozen customers; 75mW CW laser potential production start late calendar 2027

THE NPO / SCALE-UP THESIS AND THE III-V ROADMAP: SiPho pluggables (800G/1.6T) have 'for the most part ALREADY REPLACED COPPER for scale-out connections outside the rack'; the NEXT FRONTIER IS SCALE-UP, where Tower has SEVERAL NEAR-PACKAGED-OPTICS (NPO) DEPLOYMENTS PLANNED OVER THE NEXT YEAR and many more in design — NPO expected to be 'in the TENS OF PERCENT' of SiPho shipments by H2 2027 (it reuses the pluggable ecosystem, easing hyperscaler reliability/serviceability/multi-source concerns). Content growth comes from HETEROGENEOUS INTEGRATION: III-V-on-silicon INTEGRATED InP LASERS (several tens of $M of revenue expected in 2027; chip-to-wafer bonding moving in-house), die-to-wafer/wafer-to-wafer bonding, and next-gen modulators (400G/lane silicon with Coherent; TFLN and InP in development); multi-year IQE EPI SUPPLY AGREEMENT resolved the InP-substrate crunch. SiGe: 100G/200G-per-lane drivers and TIAs in HVM across all three 200mm fabs (pluggables + LPO/LRO), 400G/lane next with tight EIC-PIC co-design. Adjacent read-through: image-sensor demand SURGING for machine-vision inspection driven by 'the accelerated build-out of DDR and HBM MEMORY ASSEMBLY LINES.'
NPO = tens-of-% of SiPho shipments by H2-2027; integrated InP lasers = tens of $M in 2027; pluggables already displaced copper for scale-out

→ Coherent: Joint OFC announcement with Coherent of a 400G-PER-LANE MODULATOR IN SILICON — the next-generation figure-of-merit work (alongside Tower's thin-film lithium-niobate and InP modulator development) that anchors multi-generation exclusivity-style engagements.

Silicon photonics revenue reported within comms infrastructure and data center is now expected to MORE THAN DOUBLE in 2026 versus the prior year. GF secured 7 new optical networking design wins in Q2 across both pluggable transceiver suppliers and major hyperscaler and networking players, and is actively engaged with 4 OF THE TOP 5 optical transceiver players. Pluggables contribute the vast majority of silicon photonics revenue today. High-volume manufacturing of 200-gig-per-lane technology is underway, 400-gig capability has already been demonstrated, and the multiyear roadmap advances module enablement to 1.6T, 3.2T and beyond. GF has more than 40 silicon photonics customers, and CEO Tim Breen said GF is on track and potentially ahead of the growth targets set for end-2028 through 2030. He also cited an expectation that 70% of data center links will be optical by 2030, calling that 'perhaps even conservative' given scale-up as well as scale-out penetration.
Silicon photonics revenue to more than double in 2026; 7 new design wins in Q2; engaged with 4 of top 5 transceiver players; >40 SiPho customers; 200G/lane in HVM, 400G/lane demonstrated

Silicon germanium is OVERSUBSCRIBED THROUGHOUT 2027 and, notably, GF's SiGe business is LARGER THAN ITS SILICON PHOTONICS BUSINESS TODAY. GF secured multiple new SiGe TIA and driver design wins across networking customers in the quarter. The growth has two compounding drivers: the shift to optical networking itself, and the fact that what could previously be done in CMOS at 50-gig and 100-gig per lane cannot be done at 200-gig and definitely not at 400-gig per lane, forcing transimpedance amplifiers and increasingly the drivers out into high-performance analog processes like SiGe. High-performance analog also appears in near and co-packaged optics depending on architecture. GF is expanding SiGe capacity at Burlington, Vermont and qualifying 300-millimeter SiGe in Singapore for additional capacity, better economics and higher fT/fMAX performance. The SiGe lineage traces to IBM Microelectronics, which invented SiGe and is part of GF today.
SiGe oversubscribed throughout 2027; SiGe business larger than silicon photonics today; Vermont capacity expanding, 300mm SiGe qualifying in Singapore

Communications, Enterprise and Data Center (CED) revenue was $101.2 million, up 181% year-over-year and 34% sequentially, crossing $100 million in quarterly revenue for the ninth consecutive quarter of triple-digit growth, reflecting demand for precision timing across AI infrastructure including optical modules, switches, accelerators and related high-performance systems; CED is expected to post triple-digit growth again in Q3.

First growth driver is bandwidth: the move to 1.6T optical modules; in 2027 SiTime expects its 1.6T revenue to grow by 100% while 800G also grows significantly, in applications expected to be a combined $450 million of SAM in 2027 where SiTime has significant market share — share and ASPs are significantly higher on 1.6T than 800G because these modules need higher frequencies and performance.

DATA CENTER IS NOW ~50% OF NSE REVENUE - AND IT IS ALL OPTICAL. CEO Khaykin sized the segments for the first time this precisely: data center ~50% of NSE, aerospace & defense ~17%, the rest service provider. 'Pretty much when we talk about data center, it's all optical' - optical in R&D/lab, optical for PRODUCTION test, optical for fiber monitoring and build-out - 'there's very little copper or anything, if anything at all'. CALL — THE FIBER-CONTENT-PER-GPU FRAMEWORK (the definitive supply-side math for optical in AI factories). Base case: enterprise grows at the rate GPUs grow; THREE drivers add on top. (1) CLUSTER SIZE: clusters ABOVE ~130,000 GPUs exceed a 512-radix switch's two-layer span and need a THIRD OPTICAL LAYER -> ~50% MORE CONTENT PER GPU for very large clusters. (2) BANDWIDTH (doubles ~every 2 years): Hopper -> Blackwell kept 100G SerDes so fibers went 8 -> 16 per GPU (content DOUBLED); the RUBIN era jumps SerDes to 200G with lane count flat -> NEUTRAL; Feynman (~2029-30): fibers double again IF SerDes stays 200G, neutral if 400G arrives (BiDi/WDM could offset) — Springboard conservatively assumes NEUTRAL. (3) SCALE-UP, today 100% COPPER: Vera Rubin Ultra NVL576 is a HYBRID step — copper inside each 72-GPU rack, DIRECT OPTICAL rack-to-rack. Bracketing a full-optical scale-up: 14.4 Tbps scale-up / 200G = 72 lanes x 2 fibers = 144, plus scale-out 1.6 Tbps / 200G = 16 fibers -> 160 FIBERS PER GPU = 10x today's 16-fiber scale-out-only content (reality lands between; % of optical ports is confidential). COMBINED: optical content per GPU +1.3-1.5x BY 2028 and 'much, much higher' toward 2030. Status: Q2 enterprise strength is 'ALL JUST SCALE-OUT — we are not yet seeing scale-up or photonics in our results'; orders accelerating; 'if we could make more, we could sell more.'
Content/GPU drivers: 3rd optical layer >130k GPUs (+50%); Blackwell 16 fibers; full-optical scale-up = 160 fibers/GPU (10x); +1.3-1.5x by 2028

1.6T optical-module PCB: current orders are mainly 1.6T high-speed optical-module boards; 2026 optical-module related revenue is guided to double, 1.6T keeps growing sharply in 2027 and becomes the main shipping spec in 2028, and 3.2T boards are already being sampled. Customers are already pre-booking 2027 capacity; target is to become the world's largest high-end optical-module PCB supplier in 2027. 800G-and-above optical-module boards require M7-class ultra-low-loss laminate (1.6T effectively mandates it); management says roughly 20 players claim to be entering optical modules but few master M7 high-layer board production, which is why Zhen Ding's substrate-derived M7 technology gave it the 1.6T breakout. 1.6T optical-module board yield is described as industry-leading at above 90%, including the newly ramped Thailand lines.
