Asked whether hyperscalers are willing to absorb cost overruns above budgeted amounts for AP1000s, he said he did not want to get ahead of a firm conclusion but 'yes, we are having conversations with them in terms of what role they can play.'

SOUTHERN POWER TOLLING AGREEMENTS ROLLING OFF ARE BEING RE-AIMED AT HYPERSCALERS. As existing tolling agreements expire, Womack said the team is in the midst of recontracting conversations with a host of counterparties, screened for creditworthiness, and sees upside in pricing versus where the contracts were originally struck - contributing to the durability and length of the long-term plan. Poroch added that conversations with both current and new Southern Power counterparties are 'proving to be very fruitful', covering repricing of expiring contracts into the next decade plus the previously announced uprate/brownfield opportunities, with an update expected later in the year; the business will not 'build something and see who shows up.'

Johnson Controls introduced an AI FACTORY ABSORPTION CHILLER REFERENCE DESIGN GUIDE, which it says demonstrates how advanced thermal management can REDUCE COOLING ELECTRICAL DEMAND BY APPROXIMATELY 44% by converting waste heat into productive cooling. Because those savings free power for compute without increasing on-site generation, management claims the potential for BILLIONS OF DOLLARS OF ADDITIONAL REVENUE OVER THE LIFE OF A 1 GIGAWATT FACILITY for the customer. The approach builds on more than 65 years of YORK absorption innovation. Management noted thermal management can represent ABOUT A THIRD OF POWER in a data center, so multiple percentage points of thermal efficiency are very meaningful - and that what JCI is working on 'goes well beyond a couple of percentage points.' Efficiency now matters more because power availability constrains where data centers can be sited.
Absorption chiller reference design cuts cooling electrical demand by ~44%; thermal management is ~1/3 of data center power

CDU shipments start this quarter; CDU pipeline reached $1B; NVIDIA certification received

Air handling demand continues with the Silent-Aire franchise increasing, CDUs become more important as liquid cooling is implemented, and controls matter as well. The strategy is explicitly to keep increasing DOLLARS PER MEGAWATT across the whole thermal management chain - including the Armada modular container, which is 'loaded with everything we make.'

At the Airside Center of Excellence, applying the business system MORE THAN QUADRUPLED CAPACITY on the computer room air handler line WITHOUT SIGNIFICANT CAPITAL INVESTMENT, while achieving 100% on-time delivery, halving customer lead times, shrinking manufacturing floor space by more than 30% and cutting inventory by 50%. Management endorsed as 'a fair characterization' the view that high-capacitance MLCC demand ramping alongside next-generation AI servers will force conversion of mid/low-end capacity and put shortage pressure on the rest of the portfolio - part of its customer conversations already cover securing that non-AI piece too, with peers also raising MLCC utilization. In notebooks, new tantalum packaging offering higher capacitance in a smaller package positions a laptop recovery as more of a 2027 story.

data center orders up 4x YoY; total orders +40%; backlog over $8 billion (+40% YoY, +20% QoQ), 40% of Commercial backlog is data centers

share ~10% moving to 15%-20%; CSA Commercial margins mid to high teens

MEMORY-RELATED NET SYSTEM SALES NOW GUIDED TO GROW OVER 75% IN 2026 — memory was 49% of Q2 net system sales (EUR 6.6B total). Driver per CEO Christophe Fouquet: 'the supply challenges driving up both DDR AND HBM PRICES have prompted significant investments in fab expansion', with customers adding meaningful capacity this year AND planning MULTIPLE MEGA FABS that come online in phases over the coming years. Growth is a combination of (1) much higher VOLUME for both HBM and DDR — 'HBM will require more wafer, there's a volume effect' — with some product mix shifting toward DDR on very strong DDR pricing, and (2) rising LITHO INTENSITY as customers migrate to advanced nodes: the 1c node ('going to be enormous') and 1b use more EUV layers, with Low-NA EUV growth driven by replacing multi-patterning with more cost-effective SINGLE-EXPOSE EUV, plus more immersion DUV. Fouquet: 'this combination which create a bit the perfect storm for ASML on DRAM this year and most probably the next few years to come.' Company-wide: Q2 net sales EUR 9.3B above guidance, FY2026 raised to EUR 43-45B; ~65 Low-NA EUV systems shipping in 2026 with 2027 Low-NA EUV nearly sold out and capacity being raised ~30%.

THREE-TIER DEAL MODEL made explicit. (1) MID-TERM core AI cloud contracts of one to three years — four landmark deals closed in Q2 with REFLECTION, COHERE, an unnamed scale U.S. Neolab and a large U.S.-based quant trading firm, averaging MORE THAN $1B EACH at a yield of $20-25M PER MEGAWATT, upfront payments covering 50-60% of associated capex and payback under two years. (2) SHORT-DURATION capacity of up to six months for time-boxed needs (large training runs before a model release, RL post-training sprints) on dedicated GB300 clusters, being negotiated at $40-50M PER MEGAWATT 'and sometimes above' — roughly double the mid-term yield; one such deal signed recently. mid-term $20-25M/MW vs short-term $40-50M/MW; could sell out 2027 today but choosing not to

CALL — THE FIBER-CONTENT-PER-GPU FRAMEWORK (the definitive supply-side math for optical in AI factories). Base case: enterprise grows at the rate GPUs grow; THREE drivers add on top. (1) CLUSTER SIZE: clusters ABOVE ~130,000 GPUs exceed a 512-radix switch's two-layer span and need a THIRD OPTICAL LAYER -> ~50% MORE CONTENT PER GPU for very large clusters. (2) BANDWIDTH (doubles ~every 2 years): Hopper -> Blackwell kept 100G SerDes so fibers went 8 -> 16 per GPU (content DOUBLED); the RUBIN era jumps SerDes to 200G with lane count flat -> NEUTRAL; Feynman (~2029-30): fibers double again IF SerDes stays 200G, neutral if 400G arrives (BiDi/WDM could offset) — Springboard conservatively assumes NEUTRAL. (3) SCALE-UP, today 100% COPPER: Vera Rubin Ultra NVL576 is a HYBRID step — copper inside each 72-GPU rack, DIRECT OPTICAL rack-to-rack. Bracketing a full-optical scale-up: 14.4 Tbps scale-up / 200G = 72 lanes x 2 fibers = 144, plus scale-out 1.6 Tbps / 200G = 16 fibers -> 160 FIBERS PER GPU = 10x today's 16-fiber scale-out-only content (reality lands between; % of optical ports is confidential). COMBINED: optical content per GPU +1.3-1.5x BY 2028 and 'much, much higher' toward 2030. Status: Q2 enterprise strength is 'ALL JUST SCALE-OUT — we are not yet seeing scale-up or photonics in our results'; orders accelerating; 'if we could make more, we could sell more.'
Content/GPU drivers: 3rd optical layer >130k GPUs (+50%); Blackwell 16 fibers; full-optical scale-up = 160 fibers/GPU (10x); +1.3-1.5x by 2028

~7 gigawatts of installed Supercharger power available for distributed AI compute

Optimus 4 aspiration ~10 million units a year vs ~1 million units a year for Optimus 3

FY2027 optical >$600M; first 1.6T DSP revenue later this fiscal year; first SiPho PIC revenue in Q1; two major PIC design wins for FY2028 ramps

NPO scale-up design wins confirmed, ramping fiscal 2028; 10x density improvement needed vs scale-out

Content/transceiver high-single-digit $ → $80-90 at 3.2T; CW laser revenue starts H1 FY2028

800G+1.6T scaling concurrently on 224G DCAs; 3.2T engagements live; first 220GHz LCA

Electronic Industrial Solutions Group delivered a record quarter, and SEMICONDUCTOR was itself a record, driven by ongoing CAPACITY EXPANSION FOR ADVANCED NODES, HIGH-BANDWIDTH MEMORY AND SILICON PHOTONICS. Automotive and energy orders grew solid double digits on software-defined vehicle architectures, in-vehicle network and cybersecurity test, and grid/high-power-charging validation.
EISG record $501M (+21%); semi record on advanced nodes + HBM + SiPh wafer test

Keysight's semiconductor WAFER TEST technologies are seeing significant capacity expansion across all of those dimensions at once, and management says the forecasts for wafer fab equipment and capital going into those markets 'continues to expand'. EISG semi a RECORD; wafer-test capacity expanding across advanced nodes + memory + SiPh

INDIUM PHOSPHIDE IS THE PRIMARY CONSTRAINT on the whole business — 'we're not constrained in assembly and test capacity right now... we're really just constrained by the ramp of the indium phosphide production.' Internal InP output capacity doubles YoY by the end of the current quarter, ONE QUARTER AHEAD of the original plan, and is on track to MORE THAN DOUBLE AGAIN by the end of calendar 2027; substrates and other critical inputs for that ramp are already secured, and capacity beyond 2027 is being planned. Concrete measure: Coherent produced about 80% MORE indium phosphide lasers in the June quarter than a year earlier — those lasers feed 800G and 1.6T transceiver shipments in the current quarter, so management expects data-center revenue growth this quarter to EXCEED 80% YoY. Six-inch lines in TEXAS and SWEDEN are producing EMLs, CW lasers and photodiodes with yields that exceed the 3-inch lines across all three device types; a third 6-inch location in ZURICH starts in the first half of calendar 2027. Six-inch economics: 4x the output per wafer at half the cost.
InP output 2x YoY (a quarter early), 2x again by end-CY2027; June-qtr lasers +80% YoY; 6-inch = 4x output at half the cost

Integrated optics: CPO, NPO and other forms represent MORE THAN $15 BILLION of incremental addressable market. At ECOC in September (launch event September 21) Coherent unveils COHERENT PHOTONLINK, a complete integrated-optics platform spanning the full optical signal chain — light generation, beam shaping, transmission, detection and conversion back to an electrical signal for the XPU or switch chip — supporting CPO, NPO and other optical integration. Initial PhotonLink-related revenue begins in the DECEMBER QUARTER. Engagement intensity with customers on CPO and/or NPO 'has really gone up over the last three to six months', with almost every large strategic customer running a CPO or NPO project (some both). Content per socket is COMPARABLE between CPO and NPO — 'just a different attach point' — because Coherent supplies the laser, external laser module, isolators, polarization-maintaining fiber, full fiber-attach kit assembly and SiPho PICs rather than a single ingredient. CPO for SCALE-UP applications starts generating revenue in the second half of calendar 2027; the CPO ramping now goes first into scale-out. The 200G VCSEL is expected to be adopted in NPO/integrated-optics applications.
integrated optics >$15B incremental TAM; PhotonLink unveiled Sept 21, first revenue Dec quarter; CPO scale-up revenue 2H CY2027

800G+ switch revenue on track to double in 2026; CPO switch volume production and shipment from Q3

CW laser strategy expanded materially. The new 200G-per-lane CW laser chip has a significantly reduced die size, is more efficient, and delivers margins accretive to long-term financial targets; Lumentum is commanding a significant price premium versus market price because tight spec width produces superior transceiver yields at customers. The margin gap between CW and EML 'has closed considerably' since the prior call (EML still better). Better-than-expected output in Japan is being allocated to CW, and Lumentum is now shipping CW lasers in a relatively meaningful way into the 200G-per-lane silicon photonics opportunity, on top of internal deployment in its own transceivers.
200G CW laser: smaller die, price premium, margin gap to EML closed considerably

Technology roadmap view: silicon photonics is a viable solution at 1.6T and CW lasers are taking a significant portion of transceiver output, but at 3.2T silicon photonics 'loses some of its advantages' and Lumentum expects EMLs to come back in a meaningful way. Wupen Yuen added that in a supply-constrained environment customers will use whichever laser source they can get, so the EML-versus-CW mix is a supply/demand dynamic as much as a technical one. CPO remains the natural end state - optics placed directly on the substrate or interposer for maximum power efficiency through foundry-level advanced packaging.
SiPho viable at 1.6T; EML expected to return at 3.2T; CPO the end state via foundry advanced packaging

SCALE, described as the industry's first OCI MSA compatible solution for near and co-packaged optics, has 7 ACTIVE ENGAGEMENTS with leading companies. To secure sufficient capacity when demand is high, Marvell has entered into a capacity reservation agreement with TSMC under which it agreed to make substantial advance payments in exchange for wafer capacity over a multi-year period; it is required to purchase specified target quantities of wafers during the term and may forfeit a proportional portion of its advance payments if it does not meet them.

Compute pricing has re-rated sharply. THREE-YEAR CONTRACT PRICING IS UP ABOUT 125% SINCE NOVEMBER and five-year pricing up about 70%. Recent three-year contracts are pricing IN EXCESS OF $20 MILLION PER MEGAWATT of IT load - paying back the compute investment in around two years - while active discussions are now at AROUND $25 MILLION PER MEGAWATT, described as consistent across live customer conversations with continued upward pressure and very strong competitive tension for near-term megawatts. Recent customer prepayments are funding 45% TO 55% of GPU capex. Management stressed these are three-to-five-year deals, not two-year or spot capacity, and that it is deliberately NOT sitting on capacity to time a spot price; shorter-duration and on-demand sit above this as further upside in due course. Pricing is described as consistent globally, with possible additional scarcity in Spain and Australia from sovereign AI demand. CEO Daniel Roberts noted the announced pricing relates to GPUs ordered some time ago, so it reflects genuine price increases rather than pass-through of GPU cost inflation.
3-year contract pricing +~125% since November, 5-year +~70%; recent 3-year deals >$20M per MW of IT load, active discussions ~$25M per MW; prepayments funding 45-55% of GPU capex

SUPPLY POSTURE: above-seasonal growth for NINE straight quarters with a tenth guided. Inventory rose $83M sequentially building strategic die bank, exiting fiscal Q3 with RECORD balance-sheet inventory plus increased distributor inventory - yet days declined to 156 and channel weeks fell BELOW the six-to-seven week target. No restocking activity seen: customers continue to run very lean and most of the business is still shipping well below historical consumption levels. Industry-wide there are 'some soft spots and lead times have started to extend,' but ADI's own lead times are being kept in check. Capacity is being added by installing new tools in available space plus sourcing more external wafers, with scenario planning underway for capacity beyond current plans and joint long-view planning with front-end and back-end partners across nodes from ~6 micrometer down to 5nm/3nm. FY2026 CapEx still expected within the 4%-6% of revenue long-term model.
Inventory days 156; channel weeks below 6-7 target; 9 straight above-seasonal quarters; CapEx 4-6% of revenue

Component supply remains tight: demand for certain components is higher than available supply and the supply chain team is working to mitigate it, though Fabrinet has continued to get its share of what it needs. Management declined to name specific parts, citing three-way customer/supplier relationships on high-profile components, and confirmed that any potential supply gaps are already factored into the Q1 guidance and growth expectations for all three revenue categories.

On the proposed U.S. ban on new Chinese transceivers: not a done deal and early days, but Fabrinet does not manufacture for any Chinese providers and is focused on Western providers, so in theory it should be a positive - as long as materials and components are available. Grady cautioned that a large share of transceivers going into data centers today come from China, so an outright ban would bring the whole industry to a halt.

Highly confident in securing another major hyperscaler CSP customer in the near future; largest-customer revenue concentration may exceed 60% or 70% of total revenue and diversification realistically requires winning one specific other hyperscaler. Two ARM-based CPU programs (one server CPU, one consumer CPU, current generation N5) are in mass production with shipment volume up meaningfully, supported by the ongoing global CPU supply shortage; automotive ADAS program in China is the second-largest revenue contributor with the next-generation chip taping out late Q3 or early Q4.

Half-year report (08-14-2026), memory demand and order book: Q2 2026 memory demand was led by AI applications, and as Agentic AI spread the major hyperscaler customers kept submitting ADDITIONAL supply requests for AI-driven memory. In H2 the company expects hyperscaler infrastructure investment for AI market share and the acceleration of Agentic AI to keep demand strong for general-purpose computing servers as well as AI servers; mobile/PC demand is slowing on set-price increases, but incremental server DRAM/SSD and HBM demand will more than offset this, so the filing states the supply-demand GAP WILL WIDEN THROUGH NEXT YEAR (2027). In Q2, within the given production capacity, sales were focused on server applications with strong demand momentum: both DRAM and NAND achieved RECORD BIT SHIPMENTS and the server share of bit shipments hit an all-time high; HBM4 supply was expanded and the company was first in the industry to ship HBM4E samples to key customers. AI / HBM framing in the half-year report (2026-08-14): the memory market is leading semiconductor growth on AI and big-data demand, and the equipment market is expected to keep growing over the medium-to-long term on the aggressive DRAM-centric investment memory makers are making to break the HBM SHORTAGE caused by the explosive expansion of AI end-markets. 2022-2024 is described as a harsh down-cycle (memory price collapse, utilisation drop); 2025-2030 is framed as a structural growth phase driven by generative-AI infrastructure build-out, led by HBM and sub-2nm foundry rather than commodity products. The AI-accelerator and HBM demand surge is forcing the equipment market onto a single high-end track where marginal technology or adequate tools have no place; foreign vendors from the US, Japan and Netherlands still hold the largest shares but Korean localisation is rising and the company's tools are now in mass-production lines of major customers at home and abroad, with overseas sales rising (China semiconductor revenue KRW 63,346M in H1 2026 vs KRW 42,017M in H1 2025).
