2nm GAA 1st gen in MP since 09-2025 (Exynos 2600 first 2nm mobile AP); 2nm 2nd gen H2 2026; 3nm 2nd gen GAA since 03-2025; 4nm HPC 4th gen since 11-2024; HBM4 base die on 4nm

2026 R&D pipeline and corporate events (half-year report): 2026 development projects - ultra-high-voltage MLCC (1000V to 1250V rated) for xEV high-voltage powertrain and EV charging CLLC resonant circuits; 35V mid-voltage and flying-capacitor MLCC for high-power fast charging; ultra-high-capacitance automotive MLCC for ADAS; industrial ultra-high-capacitance small MLCC for AI server and data-center GPU/ASIC integration; high-value FCBGA substrate for next-generation server CPU; world-first 200MP folded OIS camera module with 3-degree correction; 8MP ADAS/SVS camera module. 2025 projects included FCBGA for high-performance AI accelerators (entry into AI/HPC market), server CPU FCBGA, ARM-based CPU embedding substrate, AI PC CPU substrate, server ultra-high-capacitance MLCC. Package Solution strategy: expand orders for server CPU, AI accelerator, networking and xEV/ADAS FCBGA with global top-tier customers; BGA to expand high-end smartphone AP, ARM CPU and data-center SSD controller substrates. CEO compensation note cites glass substrate as a new business being pursued. Organisation: AI Solution team and an Agentic AI development task force set up; A9 Project executive appointed 2026-04-01. Corporate: cumulative voting adopted at the 2026-03-18 AGM, effective 2026-09-10; new independent directors Lee Jong-hoon and Kim Mi-young (Seoul National University materials science) elected 2026-03-18; SVIC 79 new-technology investment fund formed 2026-05-12 (KRW 29.7B commitment, KRW 3.96B paid); FY2025 dividend KRW 2,350 per common share (payout 25.2%) paid after 2026-03-18 approval, policy to keep payout at 20% or above; board reviewing use of 2,000,000 treasury common shares; total shareholder return for H1 2026 stated as 754.8% (common share price rose from KRW 266,000 low in January 2026 to KRW 2,270,000 high in June 2026). Discontinued communication-module business (decided 2024-09-30) is now immaterial.
2026 pipeline: 1000-1250V xEV MLCC, AI server/data-center GPU-ASIC ultra-high-cap MLCC, next-gen server CPU FCBGA; cumulative voting effective 2026-09-10; FY2025 DPS KRW 2,350 (25.2% payout)

AI / data-center specific statements (half-year report): MLCC demand rising as automotive electrification and AI-server proliferation raise power consumption, increasing MLCC count per set and demand for high-temperature/high-voltage/high-reliability parts; company supplies ultra-small (0402, 0.4mm x 0.2mm) and ultra-high-capacitance MLCC and will expand global share through timely response to AI/server, networking and power products for data centers. Package substrate: demand for large-area, high-layer-count advanced package substrates keeps rising with AI accelerators, server CPUs and networking chips; FCBGA is evolving from a connection function to improving processor performance; the division has shifted its portfolio to high-layer, high-value products for servers, AI accelerators, networking and automotive, pushing high layer count, large area, thinness and finer line width with warpage-control and fine-line technologies; BGA targets data-center SSD controller and ARM CPU substrates. Package Solution head Joo Hyuk's H1 2026 incentive was tied to server/AI package substrate development and customer expansion. Optical: camera modules for humanoid robots and automotive listed as growth applications.
AI server / data-center MLCC and AI accelerator / server CPU / networking FCBGA named as the growth drivers; package substrate utilisation 89%, division OP up 3.4x YoY

Technology: Signetics has secured mass-production infrastructure for Recon flip chip, its premium high-value package type, and for Advanced SiP modules, and is investing in and developing LAB (Laser Assisted Bond) technology to win new SiP, large-body and fine-pitch business as devices get lighter and more multi-functional. Its 7nm silicon-node package has completed qualification and is in mass production, the 5nm silicon-node package has completed process and sample development, Cu pillar plus non-SOP packages have been developed to 70/65/60um fine pitch, and 3D AOI detection has been extended from 12um to 4um
7nm package qualified and in mass production, 5nm package sample development complete; Cu pillar non-SOP fine pitch to 60um; 3D AOI detection 12um to 4um

Outlook: management ties packaging demand to wafer output from Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and TSMC, which must be assembled and tested to end-user specification, and says rising integration and miniaturisation are pushing up packaging difficulty, expensive equipment investment and the need for skilled staff — raising the entry barrier for new players. Signetics is steering away from low-margin, share-losing PDIP and SOIC work toward higher-value FBGA and eMCP CSP-family products, and its expanded flip-chip line is contributing materially to revenue; it is also diversifying with Chinese-region fingerprint-sensor customers Focaltech, Goodix and A-ker and US customers Maxlinear and Movandi through its Santa Clara office

Submarine cable and HVDC build-out: submarine plant 1 reached full completion in June 2025 and is running; submarine plant 2, equipped with a vertical continuous vulcanisation line for 640kV HVDC submarine cable, broke ground in September 2025. The company has spent about KRW 469 hundred million on the cable-laying vessel and about KRW 2,200 hundred million on submarine plant 1, and plans about KRW 7,200 hundred million in total for plant 2, of which about KRW 4,972 hundred million covers the first expansion phase, with payback expected in 2034. An HVDC test centre of about 7,000 square metres was completed inside the Dangjin cable plant in January 2026, a second dedicated cable-laying vessel was acquired in May 2026, and the Vietnamese plant Daehan Vina began construction of an extra-high-voltage cable line in March 2026. Certifications in the half include a 320kV voltage-source HVDC 3000 square millimetre PQ test and a compact 320kV type test, both KEMA-certified; the 2025 R&D list also includes localisation of a Samsung Electronics equipment-control cable (S-ATC 22AWG).

Submarine plant 2 total investment about KRW 7,200 hundred million (phase 1 KRW 4,972 hundred million); HVDC test centre about 7,000 square metres completed January 2026; 320kV HVDC 3000 square millimetre KEMA certifications

Demand outlook (section II-7): the filing states that growth in AI and data centres is raising electricity demand and expanding transmission, distribution and substation investment, citing the IEA estimate that global data centres consumed about 415TWh in 2024, roughly 1.5% of world electricity, after about 12% annual growth over five years, and arguing that this raises the need to relieve grid bottlenecks and add interconnection equipment, lifting demand for extra-high-voltage cable and transmission and distribution infrastructure. Korea's 11th Basic Plan for Electricity Supply and Demand projects power demand growing about 1.8% a year to 129.3GW by 2038 with renewables at 29.2%, driven by advanced industry, data centres and electrification. The company sizes the global submarine cable market at about KRW 6.5 trillion in 2024 rising to about KRW 24.9 trillion by 2030, an oligopoly led by Prysmian, Nexans and NKT.

Global data-center power consumption about 415TWh in 2024 (about 1.5% of world electricity, about 12% annual growth); Korean demand to 129.3GW by 2038 at about 1.8% a year; submarine cable market KRW 6.5 trillion (2024) to KRW 24.9 trillion (2030)

AI servers contributed 75% to 80% of total server revenue in each of the first two quarters, with servers stably above 80% of company revenue since Q1 and notebooks contributing only a low-teens percentage; both AI and general-purpose servers grew strongly double-digit QoQ. AI server rack ASP was roughly flat QoQ, evidence that the generation handover has transitioned smoothly, and management maintains the 2026 target of AI reaching 80% of server revenue.
AI 75% to 80% of server revenue; servers above 80% of total revenue

Q3 AI server revenue is expected to grow QoQ but at a slower rate than Q2 off the high base; the full-year target of AI server revenue doubling YoY and general servers growing double-digit is unchanged, as is the target of AI reaching 80% of total server revenue in 2026 (75% to 80% in each of the first two quarters, servers over 80% of company revenue since Q1). Notebooks: Q3 shipments guided down roughly 20% QoQ and full-year shipments down double-digit YoY as memory and CPU price hikes and shortages bite; full-year overall margins expected to hold around H1 levels. From Q3, with some customers' agreement, part of the high-value component transactions on individual AI server projects shift from a buy-and-sell to a consignment model, changing revenue recognition, easing working-capital needs and reducing the gross-margin dilution from high-priced servers.
full-year AI server revenue to double YoY; AI 75% to 80% of server revenue, 80% full-year target unchanged; Q3 notebooks down about two-tenths QoQ

AI server rack ASP was roughly flat QoQ, showing the old-to-new generation transition has completed its handover; the big revenue jump came from strong volume growth while gross margin held steady, with the dilution from high-priced racks absorbed by product-mix optimisation after the sharp ASP jump in Q1. Beyond the top-5 cloud service providers (still the main AI revenue contributors), GPU AI servers for neocloud customers and ASIC AI server projects for large CSPs are both shipping in small volumes, progress in customer diversification.

New products, R&D and corporate catalysts (DART half-year report filed 08-13-2026): R&D spend H1 KRW 29,224M = 3.12% of revenue (FY2025 KRW 48,221M / 3.42%; FY2024 KRW 23,587M / 1.92%) with 122 R&D staff and 149 registered patents. Pipeline IN DEVELOPMENT: 2.xD substrates (2.3D interposer RDL substrate and 2.1D package substrate), Glass Core Substrate / glass interposer (multi-layer glass interposer technology), Glass Core FC-BGA process, Thick-Cu substrate (70um pattern for heat dissipation), through-hole Cu filling for thermal performance, and PID material evaluation (using semiconductor RDL material as PCB dielectric). COMPLETED: High Layer Slim FCBGA (transition from high-layer ABF FCBGA to slim FCBGA), high-layer coreless, hybrid ultra-thin coreless (PPG+RCC), Cu-post / high-height Cu-post and Cu-post interposer, embedded die, embedded active + cavity, both-side cavity, AiP high-layer / mmWave AiP, RF-SiP via ALD, PMIC substrate, heatsink substrate, thermal bar/chunk via, thin-seed sputter fine-line. Patents granted in 2026 include a TGV glass substrate with resin-filled vias (03-18-2026), a heat-dissipation-via PCB (01-15-2026) and a package structure (06-04-2026). Stated strategy: shift from memory-centric products toward high-value System-IC substrates (FC-CSP, SiP module) with new customers. Market framing: Prismark (Aug 2026) puts the 2026 PCB market at USD 102.0B (+18.8%) with Packaging substrates the fastest segment at USD 19.2B (+28.9%) and Computing USD 27.9B (+25.9%); 2030 outlook USD 140.5B (10.4% CAGR). MANAGEMENT: Song Ho-geon (UC Berkeley PhD, formerly Samsung Electronics TSP) joined ~Q2 2026 as Executive CTO alongside a new manufacturing head Son Gil-dong (ex-LG) and an 'AI equipment group'; co-CEOs Jeon Young-sun and Kim Young-gu (Kim re-elected 03-26-2026 to 2029-03). An RSU plan approved 05-19-2026 grants 40,000 shares (30,000-60,000 depending on 2026 operating-profit attainment vs plan) to 16 executives, payable 2027-04 from treasury shares (58,692 shares bought 06-19~06-25-2026 for KRW 7,596M). CAPITAL STRUCTURE: the 4th CB (KRW 100B) was fully converted by 04-24-2026 (last tranche at KRW 30,276) and the 5th BW (KRW 20B) by 12-11-2025, lifting shares outstanding to 37,463,931; the 7th perpetual subordinated CB (KRW 50B, 4%, conversion price KRW 21,556, 2,319,539 shares) saw KRW 11B converted after 06-30-2026, leaving KRW 39B at the 08-13-2026 filing date (KRW 16.5B held by parent Simmtech Holdings after its 06-05-2026 call, KRW 22.5B by investors). Simmtech Holdings' stake fell to 32.43% from 33.19% after it issued exchangeable bonds on 04-22-2026. Credit rating from eCredible cut to B+ (05-08-2026) from BB- (04-14-2025) with a D cash-flow grade. Share price averaged KRW 121,314 in June 2026 (high KRW 148,700) vs KRW 50,238 in January 2026; H1 total shareholder return 190.7%.

Glass-core substrate/interposer, glass FC-BGA and 2.3D/2.1D interposer substrates in development; Slim FCBGA done; R&D KRW 29.2B (3.1% of rev); ex-Samsung CTO hired; KRW 39B perpetual CB left; rating B+ (05-08-2026)

800G is NOT rolling over as 1.6T ramps — Coherent expects 800G revenue to CONTINUE GROWING YEAR-OVER-YEAR through calendar 2026 alongside the rapid 1.6T ramp. Q4 data center revenue +24% QoQ and +66% YoY. Indium phosphide is the binding constraint across the portfolio (assembly and test capacity is available); June-quarter InP laser output — the lasers that feed both 800G and 1.6T transceivers — was up about 80% YoY, and internal InP capacity doubles YoY by the end of the September quarter, one quarter ahead of plan.
800G still growing YoY through CY2026; InP laser output +80% YoY; InP is the constraint

Both transceiver tiers grow together: 800G revenue continues rising year-over-year through calendar 2026 while 1.6T ramps rapidly into 2027 as adoption broadens. Q4 data center revenue +24% QoQ, +66% YoY, the third consecutive quarter of double-digit sequential growth. Supply, not demand, is the limiter — indium phosphide capacity is the primary constraint (assembly and test have headroom), with internal InP output doubling YoY by the end of the September quarter and more than doubling again by end of calendar 2027.
800G + 1.6T both growing; DC revenue +66% YoY; InP the primary constraint

OCS addressable market held at MORE THAN $4 BILLION (doubled from $2B at OFC 2026, 2030 timeframe) and management suggests even that may be conservative — applications have widened from the original scale-out focus to scale-across and now a clear path to SCALE-UP, where there are active customer engagements. OCS revenue grew sequentially in Q4 and is expected to grow significantly through fiscal 2027 as production expands across two manufacturing locations, spanning the 320x320 platform and other system sizes. 1.6T transceivers are ramping rapidly through calendar 2026 into 2027, with the ramp pulled in versus the prior quarter's assumptions.
OCS TAM >$4B and widening to scale-up; OCS revenue growing across two plants; 1.6T ramp pulled in

Segment detail. DATA CENTER AND COMMUNICATIONS segment +40% for FY2026; Q4 +19% QoQ and +59% YoY. DATA CENTER business +41% FY2026; Q4 +24% QoQ and +66% YoY — a third consecutive quarter of double-digit sequential growth, with strong sequential growth expected again in Q1. COMMUNICATIONS +54% FY2026; Q4 +11% QoQ and +56% YoY on data-center interconnect, scale-across and traditional telecom, with particular strength in ZR/ZR+ DCI transceivers, pump lasers and complex high-end optical subsystems. INDUSTRIAL was roughly flat pro forma in both FY2026 and Q4 — semiconductor and display capital equipment grew but were offset by broader industrial weakness; growth is expected to resume led by semicap, where bookings continue to strengthen. Within transceivers, 800G revenue keeps growing YoY through calendar 2026 while 1.6T ramps rapidly through the balance of 2026 into 2027, with the 1.6T ramp PULLED IN and stronger than management assumed three months ago.
Q4 data center +66% YoY, comms +56% YoY; 1.6T ramp pulled in vs 3 months ago

GB-platform demand remains very stable, and GB-series product demand is expected to continue at least into next year even as the new-generation platform ramps; overall AI rack shipment growth expectations are unchanged.

New-generation AI rack (Vera Rubin) on plan: volume production from Q3 (production preparation in Q3) with shipments starting in Q4, ramping over subsequent quarters to become the main product next year. Foxconn is still working toward roughly half of the new-platform market and argues product standardization raises rather than lowers entry barriers, favoring suppliers with scale delivery and vertical integration - its new-generation Compute Tray line reached 100% automation. Next year's overall rack volume hinges on how much CoWoS capacity the chip customers secure; the market expects CoWoS capacity to grow more than 50% next year, with final rack output depending on chip supply. GB-platform demand remains stable and GB-series demand should last at least into next year.
Rubin racks: volume production from Q3, shipments from Q4, main product next year; new-platform share target about half; market expects CoWoS capacity +50% next year; Compute Tray automation 100%

ASIC momentum: last year roughly one tenth of AI server revenue came from ASIC servers; in H1 2026 the ASIC revenue share was already slightly above last year's full-year level, with new customers and new projects added this year. Because ASIC projects mostly run on a consignment model, reported revenue understates the real business scale. Market estimates put ASIC at about 28% of AI-server shipments this year, rising toward about 40% by 2030; Foxconn targets a 40%-plus ASIC market share, offering both GPU and ASIC solutions and taking roles from modules and cooling systems to compute-tray and rack integration.
ASIC about 28% of AI server shipments in 2026 rising toward 40% by 2030 (market estimate); Foxconn ASIC share target above 40%; H1 2026 ASIC revenue share above last year's full-year level

Q3 server revenue should grow QoQ on the GB series plus B200/B300 and storage & compute servers as customers' AI infrastructure build-out continues, partly offset in computing by notebook CPU/memory price hikes and shortages. GB300's life cycle extends into next year - it will not stop when Vera Rubin comes out - so Pegatron is racing to lock in GB300 material allocations for H1 2027 business on top of orders already received and expected Q3/Q4 business; factories have been extremely busy since July-August, with delivery timed to when each customer's infrastructure is ready. Production is allocated across Taiwan, Mexico and the US (Texas) by efficiency and customer, with Southeast Asian plants completed this year as an additional lever given a competitor's server production there.

CoreWeave was the FIRST CLOUD PROVIDER TO BRING UP AND VALIDATE NVIDIA'S VERA RUBIN NVL72, using its software-defined liquid cooling and rack management. CEO Mike Intrator said Vera Rubin 'is a generation that is seeing the margin expansion right from the start,' that demand for the platform is enormous, and that much of the 5-10 percentage point contribution-margin step-up on Q2-signed contracts is coming in the Vera Rubin SKU. Pricing and margins for Blackwell and Vera Rubin SKUs are setting new highs. The first named Vera Rubin end customer is CATERPILLAR, which will use the platform on CoreWeave's cloud as its 'data factory' to train specialized models for autonomous construction equipment - physical AI training and inference at industrial scale.
First cloud provider to validate Vera Rubin NVL72; Vera Rubin driving much of the 5-10 point contribution-margin step-up

Older-generation GPU fleets are proving far more durable than expected. CoreWeave says it remains largely SOLD OUT OF PRIOR GENERATIONS of NVIDIA GPUs in addition to current SKUs, and recently signed an A100 CONTRACT EXTENDING INTO 2029 at an attractive price - for a SKU introduced in 2020. Only a very limited part of the fleet is up for renewal, and ASPs on older generations remain at or above levels seen about a year ago. Fleet coming off contract also feeds the managed inference product. Management stresses the business model does not rely on recontracting after the initial term, so any renewal or resale is incremental to returns already earned.
A100 contract signed extending into 2029 (SKU introduced in 2020); largely sold out of prior-generation GPUs

EMLs delivered another record-breaking quarter, primarily driven by 100G-per-lane devices. 200G EMLs are accelerating and now account for over 25% of total EML revenue; management expects 200G EMLs to be 50% or more of volume by mid-calendar-2027. Lumentum remains on track to deliver over 50% EML unit growth in the December 2026 quarter versus the year-ago quarter, but expects to remain significantly behind demand even at year end.
record EML quarter; 200G EML >25% of EML revenue; >50% EML unit growth by Dec-2026 quarter

Cloud transceivers: record 800G shipments in the quarter while initiating production of next-generation 1.6T modules. Transceiver profitability continues to improve on yield gains, capacity utilization, and the initial rollout of higher-ASP 1.6T units. 1.6T uptake is expected to intensify starting in fiscal Q1 FY2027 and sustain through calendar 2027, anchored by lead Tier 1 hyperscale customers rolling out custom AI clusters. Management believes Lumentum is first to market ahead of larger competitors in many instances and can hold that share advantage through the cycle, crediting its signal integrity team on difficult 1.6T designs.
record 800G shipments; 1.6T production initiated; 1.6T uptake intensifies from fiscal Q1 FY2027

LAUNCHED the complete new AMD Helios product line and the Instinct MI450 total solution this quarter (up from 'preparing' a quarter ago), building on MI350/MI355X and EPYC momentum. Helios and MI450 ship into the same DCBBS total-solution motion - liquid-cooled rack, CDU, networking, management software and lifecycle service - with capacity heading to >6,000 racks/month including >3,000 DLC racks/month at up to 250kW per rack.
Helios product line + Instinct MI450 total solution LAUNCHED

Long-term NVIDIA partnership: shipping VOLUME SKUs across the GB200 NVL72, HGX B200, NVIDIA B200 NVL4 and NVIDIA RTX 6000 Pro product lines. AI solutions were ~60% of Q4 revenue (vs >80% in Q3) on the timing of some large AI project ramps; based on backlog, >80% of revenue is expected to be AI-related going forward, and ~70% of the $60B+ of new Q4 orders is pure AI.
shipping GB200 NVL72 / HGX B200 / B200 NVL4 / RTX 6000 Pro in volume

Preparing to be FIRST TO MARKET on the Rubin generation - Rubin, Vera Rubin NVL72, Rubin HGX, Vera CPU and other high-density Vera systems - alongside the shipping Blackwell lines. Rubin and Vera platforms are liquid-cooling-ready (Vera is CPU-based and much of Supermicro's Vera volume will also be liquid cooled); DLC capacity is being built to >3,000 DLC racks/month, most lines supporting 250kW-class rack platforms. NVIDIA's Vera also anchors the emerging CPU-based AI / agentic-AI segment that Supermicro is targeting.
first-to-market target for Rubin / Vera Rubin NVL72 / Rubin HGX / Vera CPU

The HBM4 transition is a direct order driver: CEO Rafi Amit said 'the industry transition to HBM4 together with continued capacity expansion has resulted in significant orders from MULTIPLE LEADING HBM MANUFACTURERS.' In parallel, ongoing expansion of 2.5D and 3D IC packaging capacity is producing large multi-system orders from leading foundries, IDMs and OSATs. Within the HPC/AI portion of the business the two main segments are HBM and CoWoS (and CoWoS-like) applications, both expanding quickly and growing at roughly similar pace, with the faster one depending on which customers add capacity. Growth is attributed to a combination of share gains and genuine market capacity additions across HBM, CoWoS, fan-in and fan-out.

Received orders from two advanced packaging customers for the panel level horizontal plating tool, addressing both 510 mm by 515 mm and 310 mm by 310 mm panel sizes: one a production order from an existing customer in Mainland China, the second an evaluation system for a new customer in Asia. Management positions the 510 mm by 515 mm format as the one Intel pioneered and 310 mm by 310 mm as the TSMC approach, and says panel-level packaging is seen as the ultimate solution for large AI chips / CoWoS / HBM packaging across Mainland China, Taiwan, Korea and Singapore.
2 panel-level horizontal plating orders (510 mm x 515 mm and 310 mm x 310 mm)

1.6T RAMP BEGINS: full qualification of AOI's first 1.6T product at the hyperscale customer expected 'within the next couple of weeks', with 1.6T shipments starting later in Q3 - AOI says it will be the FOURTH supplier qualified at that one big hyperscale data center customer for 1.6T. The customer returns to 10%+ of revenue in Q3. The previously announced order is now sized at MORE THAN $200M in hand: deliveries start very late Q3, the BULK ships in Q4, with a tail into Q1 2027 (target to complete by ~Q2 2027) - and management frames it as 'just the very beginning' of significant recurring 1.6T orders. Q4 1.6T revenue commitment $70-80M (limited by MATERIAL supply, not capacity); Q1 2027 1.6T revenue targeted to DOUBLE Q4 or more. Q4 combined 800G+1.6T revenue of ~$330M confirmed 'about right, directionally'. Longer term, customer feedback points to >500,000 1.6T transceivers/month by end-2027 = $300-350M/month.
>$200M 1.6T orders in hand; Q4 1.6T $70-80M; Q4 800G+1.6T ~$330M; >500k units/mo ($300-350M/mo) by end-2027

CAPACITY RAMP: 800G/1.6T manufacturing capacity is 'approaching 200,000 units per month' now, up from ~100,000/month exiting Q1 FY2026; expected to reach OVER 650,000 pieces/month by END-2026 and OVER 930,000 pieces/month by END-2027, with MORE THAN HALF of that output from TEXAS. Texas footprint expanded to OVER 1.6 MILLION sq ft in greater Houston (vs ~900k sq ft reported at Q1 FY2026 and only ~65,000 sq ft a year ago). The 210k sq ft facility (dedicated 800G/1.6T) starts initial production LATE in Q3; moving transceiver lines out of headquarters frees that fab to expand INDIUM PHOSPHIDE wafer capacity; Pearland (construction started) and Houston buildouts come online EARLY 2027. Capacity is 'complete book already from now until Q2 next year' and customer demand runs 20-40% ABOVE planned capacity. 800G and 1.6T run on the SAME line and process (1.6T differs only in final test), so 800G->1.6T scaling needs minimal incremental investment.
~200k units/mo now -> >650k/mo end-2026 -> >930k/mo end-2027 (>50% from Texas); TX footprint >1.6M sqft; booked through Q2 2027

→ Siemens: Siemens highlighted its collaboration with Infineon: integrating Infineon silicon carbide power modules into Siemens' latest solid-state circuit breakers — described as a critical enabler for safe and reliable distribution of DC power on the road to 800-volt DC data-center architecture.

Growth catalysts: GAA sales were about JPY 5 billion in Q1 and are expected at over JPY 20 billion for FY March 2027. Advanced packaging revenue, JPY 6 billion in FY March 2026, is now expected at JPY 15 billion in FY March 2027 (Q1 was JPY 4.5 billion) - a significant upward revision from the JPY 6 billion prior plan, driven by both rising customer CapEx and additional POR wins for its film deposition technology. In NAND, demand-supply is not fully adjusted - memory players are allocating clean room to DRAM while NAND wafer output needs to increase - so greenfield NAND investments are expected to resume, which converts all of Kokusai's PORs to sales and is broadly favorable. In DRAM, the D1C transition is complete and D1D is progressing. NAND sales could approach record highs, and DRAM plus NAND plus advanced packaging support growth above WFE (targeting more than a 20% sales increase).
GAA JPY 5 billion in Q1, over JPY 20 billion FY March 2027; advanced packaging raised to JPY 15 billion FY March 2027 from JPY 6 billion in FY March 2026

Revenue associated with ADVANCED LOGIC MORE THAN DOUBLED SEQUENTIALLY in Q2 as customers expanded production capacity, with demand stretching across product lines and divisions. The VeraFlex XPS materials-metrology platform kept gaining traction, driven by 'proliferation in gate-all-around manufacturers' as customers continue to INCREASE THE NUMBER OF VERAFLEX TOOLS PER FAB; XPS adoption is rising in logic, especially at the advanced nodes. Nova's AI-enabling modeling solution, combining physics-based and machine-learning algorithms, helps customers address the complex 3D device structures of gate-all-around and plays an increasingly important role in managing Nova's expanding GAA install base. An analyst characterised Nova as holding a position across ALL FOUR gate-all-around players and management did not dispute it, while declining to discuss any customer by name.
Advanced logic revenue more than doubled QoQ; VeraFlex tools per fab increasing at gate-all-around manufacturers; logic and foundry 73% of Q2 product revenue

ADVANCED PACKAGING set a record and contributed nearly one-quarter - 'nearing 25%' - of overall product revenue in Q2, driven by the dimensional metrology portfolio and fuelled by customers' continued investment in advanced packaging and HIGH-BANDWIDTH MEMORY capacity to support AI-related device demand. Nova had guided advanced packaging to between 20 and 25% of product revenue for the year and now sees it 'inching towards the 25% for the year.' Management frames advanced packaging as a MULTI-YEAR STRUCTURAL growth opportunity that has gone from essentially no revenue several years ago to a meaningful contributor, now spanning optical, chemical AND materials metrology, and becoming increasingly similar to front-end manufacturing in complexity across both logic and memory. Chiplets, HYBRID BONDING, PANEL-LEVEL PACKAGING and 2.5D integration all increase both the number of measurements required and their criticality; hybrid bonding is described as 'an additional layer that will accelerate this growth for Nova.'
Advanced packaging a record at nearly 25% of Q2 product revenue, inching toward 25% for the full year (initially guided 20-25%)

Memory and others was 27% of Q2 product revenue and Nova projects MEMORY AT ABOUT 30% for full-year 2026, a slight increase on the 70/30 logic-to-memory ratio of 2025, against a long-term model of about 60/40 in favour of logic because process-control intensity in logic is higher. The MAJORITY OF NOVA'S MEMORY EXPOSURE IS DRAM, where demand is strong, while 3D NAND remains 'somehow muted' this year because its growth is driven by UPGRADES rather than capacity expansion - even though metrology intensity between DRAM and NAND is 'more or less similar.' Nova sells to ALL THE TOP PLAYERS IN THE NAND MARKET (positions vary by product line) and expects to benefit once NAND capacity investment returns, which management hopes will be sometime next year. Coming DRAM technology transitions - 4F-squared, 6F-squared, advanced DRAM architectures and eventually 3D DRAM - all increase process complexity and metrology requirements. A new generation of the Nova PRISM platform is targeted at advanced memory structures.
Memory 27% of Q2 product revenue and ~30% expected for 2026 (2025 was 70/30); long-term model 60/40 logic/memory; DRAM strong, 3D NAND muted and upgrade-driven

On PROCESS-CONTROL INTENSITY, management said it has to be broken down by end market because each behaves differently: LOGIC INTENSITY IS HIGHER THAN MEMORY, ADVANCED PACKAGING IS 'RAPIDLY GROWING,' and 3D NAND is currently muted in process control because its spend is upgrades rather than capacity expansion. Asked about the Terafab greenfield project, management declined to comment on any specific customer but said generically that PROCESS CONTROL INTENSITY AT THE INITIAL STAGES OF GREENFIELD FABS IS HIGHER THAN IN THE ONGOING OPERATIONS OF MORE MATURE FABS, because a new fab operator must improve time to market and reach the required yield threshold - citing the Rapidus build of a couple of years ago as an example of that pattern rather than as a Nova customer statement. The structural drivers - increasing complexity in architectures and materials - remain in place, and Nova points to customer adoption, market share gains and technology wins as its key indicators of outperformance.

800-volt DC roadmap: Siemens is shaping the path to 800V direct-current architecture required for high rack density in AI factories — adoption expected to progress IN STAGES over the next four to five years with hybrid architectures dominating early phases; AC and DC to coexist in brownfield retrofits and greenfield builds; FIRST PILOTS EXPECTED IN 2027. Siemens is helping major data-center providers design, test and deploy DC power distribution. Developed a reference architecture together with NVIDIA, nVent and Fluence across compute, cooling, power and control systems for the latest NVIDIA DGX Vera Rubin platform (goal: maximizing tokens per watt); modular automation framework with ready-to-use Simatic libraries — Siemens PLCs already automating critical OT infrastructure in several megawatt-scale data centers; collaborating with Infineon to integrate silicon carbide power modules into its latest solid-state circuit breakers for safe DC power distribution.
800V DC adoption staged over four to five years; first pilots 2027; NVIDIA/nVent/Fluence reference architecture for DGX Vera Rubin

→ NVIDIA: Siemens developed a reference architecture together with NVIDIA, nVent and Fluence across compute, cooling, power and control systems for the latest NVIDIA DGX Vera Rubin platform — goal: maximizing tokens per watt and ensuring predictable, scalable operations; Siemens built a modular, scalable automation framework on it with ready-to-use Simatic libraries.

BOYD RAISED AND THE 800V PLAYBOOK: Boyd (liquid cooling — COLD PLATES + CDUs) raised to $1.8B FY2026 revenue, up from the ~$1.7B+ trajectory flagged in Q1 ($1.5B lands in Eaton's books; Boyd did $1.1B in 2025); Q2 $432M was 20% ABOVE plan; wins on being the DESIGN PARTNER embedded in chip providers' roadmaps (first look/first bid), aerospace-grade quality at scale (smaller rivals showing 'quality issues from the get-go'), and it hands Eaton an early strategic read into chip development; joins organic growth in 2027. 800V DC: content ~$3.4M PER MW CONFIRMED 'the right number'; the customer objective is TOKENS PER MEGAWATT (~5% efficiency gain from DC conversion — 'when there's so much money involved, this is going to happen'). Eaton frames FOUR technical blocks required to win 800V — (1) medium-voltage SOLID-STATE TRANSFORMER (Resilient Power, 'clearly ahead' per hyperscaler and chip-maker feedback), (2) DC BREAKER technology, (3) power electronics/power quality (UPS), (4) COOLING (Boyd) — plus a service network that arrives 'in an hour, not days'; players missing blocks 'will have a really hard time.' Prefab/modular (Fibrebond): electrician/plumber scarcity pushes modular builds, and 800V's simpler architecture INCREASES the modular opportunity, extending Eaton from gray space into white space.
Boyd raised to $1.8B FY26 (Q2 +20% vs plan); $3.4M/MW confirmed; 800V = 4 blocks (SST/DC breaker/UPS/cooling) + service; modular expands with 800V

Advanced Solutions, which includes the Fluxless Thermo-Compression (FTC) bonding platform, recognised revenue 20% ABOVE last quarter's record. K&S is maintaining its target of OVER $100 MILLION in Advanced Solutions revenue for fiscal 2026, and for fiscal 2027 Lester Wong guided TCB revenue to a range of $150 MILLION TO $200 MILLION - significant sequential growth. The company remains closely engaged with a broad base of IDM, OSAT and foundry customers as heterogeneous packaging goes mainstream, with particular confidence in heterogeneous integration around logic for Fluxless TCB.
Advanced Solutions revenue 20% above prior record; >$100M Advanced Solutions target for FY2026; TCB guided to $150M-$200M in FY2027

Beyond thermocompression, K&S accelerated its HYBRID BONDING program over the last year and says its hybrid bonder has unique features not currently in the market; it PLANS TO DELIVER A HYBRID BONDING TOOL TO A CUSTOMER IN THE FIRST HALF OF FISCAL 2027. It is also investing significantly in a PANEL-level project, seeing a lot of interest from IDMs, foundries and OSATs because panel geometry allows many more dies on a rectangle than a circle; specific panel applications are still being scoped with customers. Management frames FTC, vertical wire, direct copper-to-copper, hybrid and panel-based architectures as the emerging packaging set that will be critically necessary across a much wider array of semiconductor production, and stresses the industry is still in the relatively early stages of this More-than-Moore advanced packaging transition.
Hybrid bonding tool to be delivered to a customer in H1 FY2027

NAND is turning: MKS saw increased momentum in NAND UPGRADE activity in Q2 and expects it to continue, possibly better. RF power is the LARGEST PART OF THE BILL OF MATERIALS in such an upgrade, which is why MKS benefits disproportionately from upgrades. Announced NAND GREENFIELD fabs are expected to come in towards the END OF 2027 AND BEGINNING OF 2028, which would be even better because MKS would supply the rest of its semiconductor portfolio around a brand-new tool; NAND should become a bigger percentage of semi revenue in 2028. Until then the mix stays largely logic and DRAM driven.
NAND greenfield fabs expected end-2027 into 2028; NAND to become a bigger share of semi revenue in 2028

Demonstrated 2,200 volt PowiGaN technology, extending PowiGaN into application spaces traditionally served by silicon carbide and using the same proven architecture as the prior 750, 900, 1,250 and 1,700 volt nodes, with eight years of demonstrated field reliability and 1,500 volt architectures already in view. Positioned as a single-platform alternative to complex stacked-device approaches so data-center customers can adopt GaN today without being forced to change technologies on next-gen designs. Timing: it is a technology demonstration, not a launched product; data-center products would sit on the 1,500 volt roadmap, 'several years' out — 'the next couple of years before we see anything meaningful there', not the next couple of quarters.
2,200 volt PowiGaN demonstrated; products several years out (1,500 volt roadmap)

Data-center engagement runs on two tracks. (1) Main power path to the GPU — the biggest component of the projected billion-dollar data-center SAM — being developed with customers around Power Integrations' 1,250 volt GaN as a high-density alternative to stacked 650 volt designs; this track is earlier, still requires work with customers, and depends on when the 800 volt systems deploy. (2) Auxiliary power in and around the rack — switch trays, power sidecars and other high-voltage sockets — where there is 'a healthy roster of design-ins and a strong pipeline of ongoing design activity' with 1,700 volt products for 800 volt data centers, addressable with products in hand today and pointing to revenue in 2028. Broad range of ongoing customer engagements addressing 800 volt data centers; recent hyperscaler discussions confirm power remains a major challenge.
Aux-power design-ins could be revenue in 2028; main GPU power path further out

Battery energy storage: already shipping SCALE-2 gate-driver boards into battery storage systems used alongside renewable installations, and won an important new customer in Q2 — a utility-scale design at a top supplier of batteries for energy storage systems and EVs (customer not named). Rising power demands are pushing storage toward higher-voltage architectures and greater silicon-carbide adoption, which requires more advanced gate drivers. A number of customer engagements are underway for battery storage specifically targeting AI data centers, described as another element of the projected billion-dollar data-center SAM in 2030. Deployments of battery storage are expected to grow at a double-digit CAGR through 2035.
One new utility-scale gate-driver design win; billion-dollar data-center SAM in 2030

→ NVIDIA: In June, Power Integrations published two reference designs targeting NVIDIA 800 volt racks using its 1,700 volt InnoMux products. These auxiliary supplies sit on the compute tray in a native 800 volt system, powering components such as MCUs, gate drivers and op-amps, and deliver space savings of about 30% compared to discrete silicon carbide designs. Alongside the aux track, the main power path to the GPU is being developed with 1,250 volt GaN as a high-density alternative to stacked 650 volt designs. Aux-power design-ins point to revenue in 2028; the main power path depends on when the 800 volt systems deploy.
units: two reference designs; 1,700 volt InnoMux aux supplies on the compute tray; about 30% space saving vs discrete silicon carbide

First growth driver is bandwidth: the move to 1.6T optical modules; in 2027 SiTime expects its 1.6T revenue to grow by 100% while 800G also grows significantly, in applications expected to be a combined $450 million of SAM in 2027 where SiTime has significant market share — share and ASPs are significantly higher on 1.6T than 800G because these modules need higher frequencies and performance.

Content per data center: both grid-connected and behind-the-meter designs step in at 38 kV, 'very strong market for Powell'; behind-the-meter power islands 'increase the content for Powell from a Switchgear, switches, control, and services total package'. Powell is outside the data center today; the one-megawatt rack is built on DC distribution and the 800 volt design 'is going to happen', a mid-term DC-gear opportunity Powell is evaluating. Remsdaq automation boxes now used in-house for data-center power switching designs.
38 kV utility / behind-the-meter connection is Powell's market; 800 V DC in-rack designs a mid-term opportunity

Advanced nodes portfolio grew more than 20% in Q2 (Investor Day plan was ~7%): continued growth at three nanometer, emerging activity at two nanometer, really strong pull for 2 nm and 18A, and successful scale-up of HBM3/HBM4 on the memory side; advanced nodes were about 40% of the portfolio exiting the first half versus the 45%-50% Investor Day target, which Qnity expects to reach early.
advanced nodes +20% YoY; ~40% of portfolio vs 45%-50% target

New advanced packaging architectures (panel-level packaging, larger package formats, tighter lines and spaces on high-layer-count boards and IC substrates) all mean more material complexity and more material intensity, with fewer suppliers able to qualify; Qnity has incumbency with the same customers that commercialized the existing advanced packaging formats and expects more content per package as formats grow. Customer capacity expansions in advanced packaging underpin the durability of ICS growth.

Musk: 'Going forward, we've decided to build exclusively on Nvidia, because we think the Vera Rubin architecture is the best architecture. We think it's the best AI computer... We're exclusive to Nvidia.'
exclusive to NVIDIA for all future compute builds

Starmind AI satellite will be 'essentially an optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 computer'; launches begin next year and the same simplified design will be deployed on the ground as well as in orbit because it is 'a radical simplification of the normal NVL72 rack. It will cost less. It'll be more effective.'
Starmind orbital Vera Rubin NVL72 launches begin 2027
Musk's estimate of Rubin economics: 'what is my best guess for monetization per watt of, say, Rubin? My guess would be somewhere between $30 and $50.'
$30 and $50 monetization per watt of Rubin

AMD's new MI450 series is on schedule and Wistron, as AMD's main component-level supporter, sees AMD's customer forecasts growing (citing Lisa Su's optimism). Beyond components, Wistron has already taken rack/system orders for MI450 from customers ('yes'), on schedule to ship together with AMD's product ramp in H2 2026; whether Wistron builds components or full AMD systems is decided by the customer, across enterprise and CSP.

VR (Vera Rubin) is already in mass production - management confirmed it, citing Jensen - and the generation handover has caused no Q3 air pocket: some customers still prefer GB300 so GB300 volume persists, while others are moving to VR, leaving Q3 looking quite good. Wistron expects to keep a reasonable margin after the VR launch despite the higher rack price, with OP margin 'no worse than GB300' and the trend holding into H1 2027 when VR volume ramps; some new customers are starting directly on VR. Wistron is also working on the pure Vera CPU racks and switch/storage racks NVIDIA announced alongside VR, has already received orders for the new products, and will ship them in H2 2026.
→ AMD: MI450 series is on schedule; Wistron is AMD's main component-level supporter and has additionally received customer orders for MI450 rack systems, shipping when AMD's product ramps in H2 2026.

→ NVIDIA: Vera Rubin is already in mass production and Wistron ships as NVIDIA's component-level partner; Wistron has also received orders for NVIDIA's new Vera-based products (pure Vera CPU racks, switch and storage racks), shipping in H2 2026, and NVIDIA develops these new products with its small set of ODM partners.

800 V data centers: multiple low-profile modular DC-to-DC and AC-to-DC products with efficiency in the 98% range, sampled with positive feedback at multiple customers; 'We expect the initial production revenue in late 2027 and to see more meaningful ramp in 2028'; 800 V expected to coexist with 12 V and 48 V architectures; seen as an opportunity to increase content per rack. Higher power density per generation brings more dollars per rack.
800 V products: initial production revenue late 2027, high-volume ramp in 2028; efficiency in the 98% range

→ Amazon: 'We continue to add content in US hyperscalers' AI deployments with DESIGN WINS SUPPORTING AWS POWER SUPPLY AND BATTERY BACKUP SYSTEMS' — creating additional content opportunities for the high-voltage portfolio including silicon carbide as architectures move toward 800V DC.

The new Turing design center began trial operation in Q2 running small and mid-size projects and is expected to be in full use in H2; it adds some depreciation/R&D cost but is aimed squarely at 3nm, 2nm and even more advanced process work plus advanced packaging. The R&D roadmap already includes CPO, IVR (integrated voltage regulator), next-generation UCIe die-to-die, and N2-on-N2 advanced-process development; opex should grow only modestly versus a clearly larger revenue increase next year.

Capacity and technology roadmap: multi-site production at Yokkaichi (one of the world's largest flash memory bases, leading-edge R&D) and Kitakami; the K2 fab at Kitakami began operation in September 2025 and began production of the 10th generation BiCS FLASH this year. Capex plan: average JPY 470 billion annually from FY2026 to FY2028 (JPY 450 billion this year), flexible to market change and fully covered by cash flow. R&D about JPY 200 billion for the full year, concentrated on BiCS 10/BiCS 11 and AI inference SSDs (super high IOPS SSD for inference servers); UFS 5.0 new high-speed standard for edge AI / on-device AI announced. Strategy: not pursuing market share through aggressive investment - pursuing quality and profitability via higher sequential speed, energy efficiency and product quality.
Capex average JPY 470 billion/year FY2026-FY2028 (JPY 450 billion this year); R&D ~JPY 200 billion; BiCS10 in production at Kitakami K2, BiCS11 and AI inference SSD in development

AI data center applications drive the WFE market: sales to AI data center are expected to grow by five times or more in the five years from calendar 2023 through calendar 2027, spanning not only GPU and HBM but also DDR, CPU and 3D NAND. Technology transitions expected within two years: logic scaling from the 3 nanometer mainstream toward 2 nanometer with backside PDN adoption, DRAM evolving to the 1D node (1C to 1D transition), HBM stacked DRAM count rising from 12 to 16, and NAND evolving to 300 layers and further to 400 layers. Agentic AI is the driver of the overall WFE market; CY2026 WFE application mix is about 60% logic and 40% memory, versus 65%/35% last year.
AI data center WFE sales to grow five times or more CY2023-CY2027; HBM stacks from 12 to 16; NAND to 300 then 400 layers; logic mainstream 3 nanometer moving to 2 nanometer

Power electronics stable at a low level: SiC installed base underutilized, GaN utilization around 60%-70% and gradually increasing; GaN has a strong opportunity in AI data centers for 800-volt DC to DC conversion, with SiC coming first at the high-voltage entry point and GaN following with a delay; mid-term view of a GaN market 3X-ing to around EUR 450 million of tool revenue fully holds; AIXTRON systems (G5+ and G10-GaN) are the tools of record across the GaN power market, so customers are expected to arrive with multi-dozen tool orders when the wave starts
GaN installed-base utilization around 60%-70%; mid-term GaN tool revenue view around EUR 450 million

HVDC ramp: plus/minus 400V and 800V systems start mass production in Q3 2026, but Q4 shipments and full-year volume stay limited - larger volume comes next year. The plus/minus 400V architecture is being pushed more aggressively and ships more this year; 800V is driven mainly by NVIDIA and depends on when data-center operators adopt that power architecture - NVIDIA's Blackwell shipments are still much larger than Rubin, and part of the Rubin lineup can still run on low voltage. On the 110kW power shelf and other new product cycles Delta believes its market share remains high because it engages customers earliest, and the fast generational churn of AI power architecture favors its engineering resources; it declined to quantify share for the Rubin-linked 110kW PSU but asserts market leadership. A solid-state transformer (an energy gateway, not a one-for-one transformer replacement) has its first trial customers in smaller data centers, and a first small fuel-cell line starts by year-end with the first volume line planned next year, with units at Taipower and another test site performing well.
HVDC plus/minus 400V and 800V mass production from Q3, limited volume this year, ramp next year; 110kW power shelf share seen high

Liquid cooling keeps scaling: liquid-cooling products were about 10% of group revenue last year and will exceed 12% this year (an analyst cited about US$1.6 billion of Liquid-to-Air contribution last year). Management expects Liquid-to-Air to persist considerably longer than the market's assumption that Liquid-to-Liquid fully takes over around 2028.
liquid cooling about 10% of revenue last year, above 12% this year; Liquid-to-Air about US$1.6B contribution last year

Technology read-through on evolving cooling architectures: asked whether higher inlet fluid temperature specs for future GPU designs reduce chiller demand, management said demand is improving and increasing for Modine because of its free-cooling technology — a higher inlet temperature lets the unit run in free-cooling mode more of the time, driving further efficiency and reducing data-center power consumption, while the chiller and refrigerant cycle stay in place as the 'insurance policy' for temperatures above that band. Chillers support both facility cooling and incorporation into direct-to-chip liquid cooling systems — similar models and SKUs sit on the same data-center rooftop doing both — so Modine cannot split its order book between the two. The enhanced three-megawatt chiller is being introduced to customers and will raise output per line versus the 2 MW unit.
3 MW chiller launching (vs 2 MW today); higher GPU inlet temperatures increase free-cooling/chiller demand

BBU content growth with next-generation accelerators: asked about NVIDIA Rubin production starting and per-rack battery cell capacity possibly rising from 80 W to 120 W, management said the Rubin percentage will not be so high yet but Panasonic's portion will increase including capacity, and as the BBU solution evolves the unit price would go up - required output changes and the total solution expands ('it's not replacing PBU, but it's PBU plus CPU'); non-GPU demand (TPU, ASIC, including CPU racks for inference) is also expanding and is part of the JPY 550 billion full-year picture.
Per-rack battery cell capacity discussion 80 W to 120 W with Rubin; unit price to rise as BBU solution evolves

Market shift toward SPX solutions: as more liquid cooling goes under the roof, dry cooling appears to be the most favored heat-rejection solution, with adiabatic and cooling towers also in demand; SPX sees significantly increasing demand from existing hyperscalers and had nice wins with colos and neoclouds. Hyperscalers give visibility several years forward because they need SPX's product to turn the data center on and send teams of 10 people into SPX facilities for two weeks at a time.

Cooling: launched a new liquid cooling solution through JetCool and showcased next-generation power and infrastructure technologies at Computex. The JetCool acquisition brought 'industry-leading cold plate capability'; Flex then 'had to develop and introduce CDUs into the market' and is now 'in the process of qualifying those products with the right end customers to scale that business up'. Cooling inside CPI is 'still nascent' but 'will be a pretty important part of our growth strategy overall for CPI within the cloud segment' as air cooling is replaced by liquid cooling.

Integrated power + cooling + compute design is now a hyperscaler-level conversation: 'in the last few months, several hyperscaler customers at a very high level, we've had strategic conversations around power cooling and thinking about next generation silicon', with customers saying 'before we deploy the next generation silicon, we need to be thinking about power capability and power requirements' and already asking about solid-state (SST) technology. Scope named: 'sidecars on tower, cooling racks, and a fully integrated modular design'. CEO: 'that really puts us in the unique position of one of the few people who are able to do this' — power products with true IP, cooling products, plus compute integration.

High-voltage transition update: 'first is on 400 volt, which is kind of the immediate programs that we are working on, followed by 800 volt. We feel very good about the progress on those programs. Don't see any major limitations, at least to the guide we have given for 2027 and 2028', with solid-state transformer technology 'that is going to be coming our way' after that. CEO: 'Flex is kind of the leader in this transition on the embedded power side'. On components: 'there's lots of conversations about component constraints and all of that, we have planned all of that in the guide we have given. If anything, there should be some upside to that... as availability becomes better.' Updated long-term guidance around the transition comes at the November Investor Day.
400V programs ramping now, 800V next, solid-state after; component constraints already planned into the guide

→ NVIDIA: CEO cited the NVIDIA partnership as the lead example of integrated modular infrastructure: 'what we announced with Nvidia a few months ago in terms of developing an overall modular platform, which encompasses everything that we do, is a good example of a customer who's thinking about it and moving it in that direction' — a modular platform for deploying 'mini data centers' that bundles Flex's power, cooling and compute-integration content rather than a single component.

EMIB-T advanced packaging: Unimicron is one of three substrate makers (alongside two Japanese peers) qualified on the EMIB-T platform; first-phase yield target is 50%, with the customer contractually protecting supplier profitability below that yield and volume production starting next year (2027). Key EMIB-T equipment is centrally allocated among the three suppliers and second/third equipment sources are being qualified; EMIB-T-related investment is less than 10% of the raised capex and platform-dedicated equipment only 10% to 15% to 20% of that, since much of the new capacity is general FC-BGA for CPU-based inference designs that need no interposer. Management notes hyperscaler customers moving toward chiplet-style in-house designs are qualifying substrate suppliers directly and pre-booking capacity. Glass-core substrates: no volume production expected before 2029-2030, though R&D programs run with three customers, each customised. Mid-to-long-term gross-margin ambition is 50 to 60%.
EMIB-T first-phase yield target 50%, volume production 2027; EMIB-T investment under 10% of capex (dedicated equipment 10-15-20% of that); glass-core substrate volume not before 2029-2030

Ahead of schedule and currently billing for 437 MW of capacity. Billing began on 437 MW in mid-July, nearly 200 MW more than at the end of the first quarter, after substantially completing four of the five CoreWeave campuses ahead of the end-of-summer target. Management stresses that delivering hundreds of megawatts of high-density infrastructure 'requires far more than access to power' - it requires an integrated development and operating platform - and that the AMD sites are not greenfield: equipment is secured, contractors are on site across the five campuses, and at Pecos the building shell is essentially complete.
437 MW billable, nearly 200 MW more than at the end of Q1

The Bitcoin-mining-to-AI conversion is nearly complete: Core Scientific ended June with nearly 30% fewer miners online than at the end of the first quarter and is now self-mining at only two sites, running that business primarily to offset contractual power costs during the wind-down, which continues over the remainder of the year so that 2027 starts with a clean sheet of paper. Having spent the past year converting existing power capacity from Bitcoin mining to high-density colocation, the next phase complements that with selective acquisition of powered land and development of new sites: a new site pipeline of more than 2 GW of potential incremental power has been identified, with initial capacity potentially available from late 2028 through 2030, and management hopes to bring a new site to market by year-end. The Hunt County, Texas acquisition earlier this year is representative of that pipeline.
nearly 30% fewer miners online QoQ, self-mining at two sites; >2 GW new-site pipeline (late 2028-2030)

→ CoreWeave: Four of the five CoreWeave campuses were substantially completed ahead of the end-of-summer target, taking the program to 437 billable megawatts - nearly 200 MW more than at the end of the first quarter - and driving GAAP colocation revenue to $137 million. Dalton Phase II, the fifth and final campus and the last 150 MW of the CoreWeave build-out, begins delivering at the end of 2026 and is on track for full completion in early 2027. The relationship began as a 16 MW lease at the Auburn campus in 2024 and has since expanded to 590 MW of total contracted capacity; revenue is recognized straight-line over the 12-year lease terms, pulling contractual escalators forward. Auburn and Dalton become fully leased once the AMD-credit-supported neocloud leases are added.
units: 437 MW billable of 590 MW contracted; 150 MW remaining at Dalton Phase II; value: $137 million GAAP colocation revenue in the quarter

Advanced packaging (quantified as several hundred million dollars of revenue) is performing quite well with share gain in the IC substrate / package substrate part of circuitry, strong high-end paste and wafer-level packaging; Element is establishing processes of record for the transition from CoWoS to CoPoS and other emerging technologies expected to ramp about 18 months from now, and expects the advanced packaging business to accelerate into 2027 and 2028.
advanced packaging several hundred million dollars of revenue; CoWoS-to-CoPoS ramp ~18 months out

Product content for higher-capacity data centers: 'We're adapting some of our products for those applications ... our new Pin & Sleeve devices that are going to higher amperage to the 800 volt infrastructure.' Modular/factory-built trend: PCX power skids for data centers and System Control substation control houses built in a factory setting, DMC crimp connectors replacing field welds on busbar.
new Pin & Sleeve devices for 800 V data-center infrastructure

Fan-out panel-level packaging (FOPLP) for AI: chairman confirms PTI is an AMD AI-chip supply-chain partner providing fan-out PLP solutions and is actively pursuing more AMD AI-chip applications; despite equipment-delivery delays, installation issues and doing new-product qualification in parallel, the program is on schedule and PTI is confident of volume production before the middle of next year, which would make it the world's first company to mass-produce fan-out PLP for AI applications. The former-AUO fab conversion is going smoothly: floor 1 for middle-end/RDL processing, floor 2 for chip-on-panel and mounting packages onto ABF substrates; the G7 panel equipment supporting the AMD program is fully installed and in qualification, with automation being added. PTI showed an engineering sample of a 5x-reticle-size AI package (one reticle = 26x33mm) - it says only TSMC otherwise has this capability - and notes a G7 panel fits about 45 such large AI packages versus 8 to 9 on a wafer, positioning panel output as a complement to foundry wafer-based advanced packaging. FOPLP equipment lead times run about a year plus installation; management estimates a new entrant would need roughly three years from ordering to customer qualification (PTI started fan-out panel work in 2015). In high-end flip-chip BGA, PTI already mass-produces large FC-BGA/MCM and will move a large one-reticle-size chip package into volume production in Q3.
AMD fan-out PLP volume production before mid-2027 (target: world's first FOPLP for AI); 5x reticle-size panel packages, ~45 per G7 panel vs 8-9 per wafer; FOPLP equipment lead time ~1 year

Optical/CPO roadmap: the Broadcom cooperation has brought PTI into optical communications - it will build Optical Engines using its panel fan-out technology, with small-volume production of the first OBO and OSFP versions starting around end-2026; integrating the Optical Engine into a switch (a CPO switch) is targeted to start shipping in H2 2027, and integration of the Optical Engine into AI chips is expected around 2028 or later once designs mature (engineering simulations already completed). Separately, TSV interconnection for DRAM co-developed with a partner has completed DDR-5 trial production and moves to volume production and shipments in Q4 2026 - a foundation for future HBM manufacturing that management expects to start shifting DRAM packaging from 30-year-old wire-bond formats toward advanced packaging, with a meaningful revenue and margin contribution from next year.
Optical Engine small-volume production from end-2026 (OBO, OSFP); CPO switch shipments from H2 2027; AI-chip integration ~2028; TSV-based DDR-5 DRAM volume production from Q4 2026

→ AMD: Chairman: PTI has become a supply-chain partner for AMD AI chips and will provide AMD fan-out PLP (panel-level packaging) solutions, and is actively pursuing additional AMD AI-chip applications. Despite equipment-delivery delays and parallel qualification, the AMD program is on schedule; PTI is confident of volume production before the middle of next year at the converted former-AUO fab, where the G7 panel equipment supporting AMD is installed and in qualification - which would make PTI the first company globally to mass-produce fan-out PLP for AI applications.

→ Broadcom: PTI and Broadcom will form a joint venture in Singapore - a major milestone making PTI a strategic and preferred partner of Broadcom. Built on PTI's fan-out PLP AI packaging experience, the JV will co-develop and produce additive-process fine-line-width redistribution-layer (RDL) packaging directly on advanced substrates (fan-out based), and will serve Broadcom exclusively without affecting PTI's fan-out PLP work for existing and future customers. An NDA is signed and the deal awaits Taiwan investment-authority approval, after which details will be disclosed; the JV funding goes in staged installments and does not raise PTI's NT$500 hundred million capex. The cooperation also brought PTI into the optical-communications field (Optical Engine, CPO switch roadmap).

Bookings in the third quarter were strong with book-to-bill better than 1.1; Sanmina continued to secure more customer orders for the next-generation accelerated compute business in Q3 (after securing orders with both hyperscale and OEM customers last quarter), expanding its overall customer base, while the legacy accelerated compute platform at ZT Systems has gone to zero.

Sanmina's ZT Systems business (the acquisition announced in May 2025 that created its partnership with AMD) is working in very close collaboration with AMD and joint customers to support almost all pre-production activities for the next-generation accelerated compute program; these non-recurring engineering services carry little revenue but a lot of labor charges and drove the non-GAAP operating margin beat to 8.0%, though longer-term margin is still expected in the 6%-7% range.
non-GAAP operating margin 8.0% (+230 bps YoY); long-term 6%-7%

Q4 FY2026 outlook: revenue $3.3 billion-$3.6 billion (core Sanmina $2.5 billion-$2.6 billion, ZT Systems $0.8 billion-$1.0 billion) and non-GAAP operating margin 7.5%-8.0%; the ZT range is below the prior implied guidance entirely because of a few legacy programs, and the new next-generation accelerated compute program is not included in the Q4 outlook due to revenue recognition timing — it is expected to begin contributing revenue in Q1 fiscal 2027 and ramp over time.
Q4 revenue $3.3 billion-$3.6 billion; ZT Systems $0.8 billion-$1.0 billion; op margin 7.5%-8.0%

→ AMD: ZT Systems is working in very close collaboration with AMD and joint customers to support almost all pre-production activities for the next-generation accelerated compute program; orders have been secured with both hyperscale and OEM customers, with more added in Q3; production revenue is expected to begin in Q1 fiscal 2027 and ramp over time through fiscal 2027 into fiscal 2028.

→ AMD: The ZT Systems partnership with AMD dates from the ZT Systems deal announced in May 2025; the business was expected at a $5 billion-$6 billion annualized run rate in its first year, and AMD 'continues to add more customers', which management says broadens Sanmina's addressable market for AMD Helios production even though share is hard to gauge.
value: ZT Systems run rate $5 billion-$6 billion (FY2026)

HBM hybrid bonding at a decision point: evaluations ongoing at one of the three memory companies with another starting its evaluation; all three are preparing to adopt hybrid bonding at some point because the device performs significantly better and produces far less heat; H2 2026 will clarify which HBM applications (HBM4E or even HBM3) adopt the technology and at what scale; the JEDEC height relaxation does not change that characteristic

Keystone, the 100 Gb per lane 5 nm CMOS PAM4 DSP and SerDes, continues to ramp into high-volume production at major hyperscale customers across U.S. and Asia for 400 Gb and 800 Gb deployments, delivering almost 40% lower power consumption than competition; all the revenue growth now is driven by 800 Gb, which becomes substantially the bigger portion of run-rate revenue into 2027; MaxLinear says it is now designing across the board of all optical module players on 800 Gb and is one of only three PAM4 DSP players with a track record of millions of units shipped.
almost 40% lower power than competition; growth now 800 Gb-driven

Rushmore, the 1.6 Tb optical PAM4 DSP at 200 Gb per lane, is sampling with substantial performance and power advantages and a unique supply-chain diversification versus competition; it is expected to become an important optical connectivity growth driver beginning in 2027 — initial ramps at one or two opportunities in the second half of 2027, layering through 2028 and 2029 — with ASP upside at the higher speed, while the same Keystone customers are working toward deploying 1.6 Tb and 800 Gb keeps growing alongside.

Photonic SOI addresses pluggable transceivers, near package optics (NPO) and co-packaged optics (CPO); most current revenue and growth comes from scale-out, mostly pluggables, with NPO taking share and CPO expected to ramp on scale-out at the end of the year; scale-up is starting with pluggables and will move to CPO; roughly the same Photonic SOI content in all these architectures

Electrification: $2.7B of data-center orders in Q2 — >$5B in H1 2026, MORE THAN DOUBLE full-year 2025 (of ~$14B total H1 orders); segment orders +66% to $6.3B (~1.7x revenue); equipment backlog $41B (+69% / +$17B YoY; air-insulated switchgear alone ~$5B, shipments 9,000 -> ~10,500 units this year); North America equipment orders ~4x YoY (now largest region, incl. Prolec ~$900M revenue in Q2); revenue +68% reported / +29% organic; EBITDA margin 18.4% (+700bps). NEW AI-datacenter products: first 5 MW SOLID-STATE TRANSFORMER (indoor) prototype delivering to a hyperscaler (R&D-shared) later in 2026, 6 MW outdoor SST started with a DIFFERENT hyperscaler — SST orders '27+, gated by how fast AI factories shift to 800V DC; medium-voltage UPS 'stability block' could book orders even sooner (possibly H2 2026). Data-center scope today ~$300M/GW; with SST + MV-UPS entitlement is 2-3x that, expected in 2027 orders. Integrated Electrification+aeroderivative solutions seen adding up to $500M orders/year.
H1 DC orders >$5B (2x FY25); SST 5MW to hyperscaler 2026; scope $300M/GW -> 2-3x

AI chip roadmap: an upgraded AI chip that is a 'moderate improvement over AI4' probably reaches production around the middle of next year, and AI5 is hopefully in VOLUME PRODUCTION around the middle of next year, going INITIALLY INTO OPTIMUS. Musk: 'Tesla chip team is really doing great work... I think it's going to be the best edge computing chip in the world.' Tesla also intends to upgrade essentially every camera-equipped car below Hardware 4 to the next-generation AI board so they can run FSD v15 and later versions.
no specific figure (both chips targeted for production around the middle of next year)

800V DC data centers: 'We have ZERO order in the backlog for 800 volt DC data centers. Nobody has, because there is waiting for the availability of components from NVIDIA and the like.' Commercial impact seen from late 2027 or 2028 onwards; ABB building the complete 800V DC portfolio now — already a leading player in DC switches, breakers and components, expects the new architecture to shift more content to medium voltage, boosting its medium-voltage UPS. Heavy R&D allocation plus the announced acquisition of Advantics (France — DC technology, silicon carbide technology, joining Electrification for DC and data center). Dedicated DC-topic webcast announced for September 24.
Zero 800V DC orders in backlog industry-wide; commercial opportunity late 2027/2028; Advantics acquisition adds DC/SiC technology

The June 2026 presentation says data center TAM is shifting to liquid cooling: to date a vast majority of the TAM for the thermal management equipment BASX provides to data centers is cloud compute data centers cooled by air-side equipment, and by 2028 AAON anticipates the split to be 60% liquid and 40% air-cooled.
by 2028 anticipated split 60% liquid / 40% air-cooled (AAON estimate)

Capacity conversion is the swing factor for InP epiwafer supply, and it is gated on customer commitment: "We also have the ability to flex assets and convert existing tooling to support indium phosphide growth, but this would need to be tied to concrete customer commitments." On converting GaAs lines to InP: "Our tool set is flexible to some degree. We can certainly transfer or convert capacity from our technology to the next. That kind of conversion would again need to be tied to discrete customer demand and visibility to that, because obviously it does come with downtime of the tools and also CapEx commitments." On Taiwan 6-inch InP epitaxy: "We are monitoring demand very closely, and as mentioned, we are converting capacities if and when that demand materializes." Additional MOCVD tools would come via LTA, customer co-funding, or tool consignment - "any kind of capacity expansion or addition of tools will need to come with customer commitments." Wafer-diameter transitions (4->6 inch, 6->8 inch) are customer-driven, with no company-wide push.
GaAs->InP tool conversion and Taiwan 6-inch InP epitaxy, both gated on concrete customer commitments (LTA / co-funding / tool consignment)

Next-generation substrate roadmap: significantly bigger substrates integrating more chips - up to more than 40 chiplet structures on one board-like substrate the size of a laptop, with silicon-based communication structures inside so chips talk to each other like one big chip; energy supply for these super structures up to 40 kilowatts at around 0.7-0.8 volt, driving embedded high-power electronics (miniaturized silicon carbide transformers embedded in PCBs on accelerator cards); glass cores and embedded optical connections also on the roadmap, co-developed on long-term roadmaps with hyperscalers and chip producers.

Development of the next-generation Vera Rubin series is already underway in step with NVIDIA's GPU roadmap; Gigabyte expects to be time-to-market leading, with mass production currently expected to start in the second half of 2026 - final timing per NVIDIA's official announcement. Rubin platforms are positioned for next-generation training and inference and for higher-density, higher-efficiency AI infrastructure.
Vera Rubin products expected to start mass production in H2 2026 (timing per NVIDIA)

AI power content expanding: designing 800V power management for data centers; high-voltage MOSFETs used in AI power applications (strong quick-turn Asia demand); customers increasingly adding Vishay passives in AI power-management solutions — polymer capacitors, power inductors and current-sense resistors. Next-gen design focus on server power, optical communication modules and high-bandwidth network switches (incl. 800G/1.6T AI optical switches). SiC strategy: released 750V Gen2 planar MOSFETs, standing up an 8-inch SiC wafer fab at Newport; SK Key Foundry releasing products in Q3 to add AI-application capacity.
800V DC power mgmt; HV MOSFETs + polymer caps/inductors/current-sense for AI power

AMD's MI450 series is in NPI stage at Inventec alongside the NVIDIA next-gen program, with mass production expected around H2 2026 per market schedules. Inventec's initial role on MI450 is board-level provider in the initial stage, with the option to go for the full rack later if the opportunity arises; the collaboration model with former partner ZT on MI450 was left open.

Next-generation GPU server products for both NVIDIA (Rubin) and AMD (MI series) are in NPI stage at Inventec, which will match both vendors' mass-production schedules - external expectations put volume production in H2 2026 to year-end. Both L6 board-level and L10 system-level are planned, with L6 the initial focus.

800V DC architecture stance unchanged: 'We believe it's gonna come. We believe that it's gonna be more progressive than some of you expect' — Legrand sees itself well-positioned for both hybrid architectures and full DC, viewing the shift as an opportunity (more data centers, higher density, more energy efficient) rather than a threat. More detail promised at the capital markets day in Singapore on September 29, 2026, with a particular focus on data centers. In UPS, Legrand is a small player (industrial and increasingly data-center use); not a significant inverter player.

800-volt DC power architecture portfolio launching 2H 2026, shipping 2027+, for very high-density AI compute (drives liquid cooling across the full IT stack); SmartRun integrated white-space system (power distribution + liquid cooling) and One Core full-DC solution gaining traction; power modules becoming an industry standard

→ NVIDIA: Vertiv One Core selected to deliver the full data-center solution (power, thermal, IT white space, services) for Ecodata Center (Sweden) running NVIDIA's latest-generation systems; 800V DC + liquid cooling for high-density AI compute

Building on the photonics business acquired from Intel: developing capabilities across co-packaged optics (CPO), near-package optics and co-packaged copper; demonstrating system-integration at OFC 2026 with next-gen optics from 800G to 1.6T plus integrated advanced packaging and the accompanying cooling technologies. Silicon photonics cited as a margin-accretive driver of the Intelligent Infrastructure segment.

NVIDIA still leads the GPU market and will remain the larger share of Wiwynn's GPU business, but AMD is re-entering the fight with its next generation and more than one customer has approached Wiwynn about AMD GPU projects; Wiwynn will co-work with AMD from the pilot-build stage, leveraging a similar rack design across customers. The AMD rack is double-wide, also a 72-GPU configuration but with more memory content, so its price should be higher than the GB rack: against an analyst's roughly US$3.58M per GB rack reference, management indicated around US$5M for the AMD rack (with margin rate expected similar to GPU projects). Customers are still deciding how to portfolio their data centres across NVIDIA, AMD and their own ASICs.
GB rack about 358 ten-thousand US dollars per rack (analyst reference); AMD next-gen rack seen around 500 ten-thousand US dollars; 72-GPU double-wide with more memory

2026 outlook: demand remains strong for both AI and general-compute servers, with good growth expected for the full year but the momentum weighted to H2 because of the AI platform transition. AI stays above 50% of revenue (slightly above 2025's roughly half), with ASIC projects still the main AI contributor at roughly nine-tenths of AI volume. General server growth is driven by AI itself - CSPs split workloads such as agentic AI front/back-end services and part of inference onto general compute for TCO - and 2026 general server revenue and shipment units will both exceed 2025 (management suggested roughly 20-30% growth as a reference), with every quarter growing versus last year's H1-weighted pattern. Q1 2026 will certainly grow YoY, while QoQ growth off the record Q4 is challenging.
AI above 50% of 2026 revenue; ASIC about nine-tenths of AI volume; general server revenue and units both above 2025

The previous-generation GB200 GPU project has concluded - its cost structure drove the Q4 gross margin decline - and 2026 GPU efforts shift to developing the new-generation platform with customers and technology partners, with new ASIC and new GPU products both starting to ship in H2 2026. Wiwynn has been pushing customers toward a consignment model for GPU components since GPU projects began and hopes to have a definite answer by the next-generation ramp; it mostly builds to L11 for CSP customers (who handle their own integration), with L12 opportunities limited to sovereign-AI style tenders it pursues selectively after last year's project.
